candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Deep Neck Space Infection.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize fever, neck swelling/torticollis, trismus, and odynophagia as concerning for deep neck space infection (retropharyngeal, parapharyngeal, or submandibular/Ludwig's angina), requiring urgent contrast CT imaging and airway assessment given the risk of airway compromise and descending mediastinitis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Mandible Fractures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize clinical features suggesting mandible fracture (malocclusion, trismus, step deformity, numb chin) and the need for imaging and maxillofacial/plastic surgery referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply trial evidence recall reasoning for Landmark Preventive Medicine and Screening Trials.
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a description of one of the six landmark trials' methods and results (Swedish Two-County/mammography, MASS/AAA screening, COLONPREV/colonoscopy vs. FIT, NLST/lung cancer CT screening, VAXICOL/influenza vaccination of staff, BNT162b2/COVID-19 vaccine), identify the trial's principal conclusion.
candidates.study_unit: Landmark Preventive Medicine and Screening Trials

candidates.principal_decision: Apply afib acute mgmt reasoning for Cardiac Dysrhythmias (SVT, Atrial Fibrillation, Ventricular Tachydysrhythmias).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply time-since-onset and anticoagulation criteria to guide acute AFib cardioversion decisions.
candidates.study_unit: Cardiac Dysrhythmias (SVT, Atrial Fibrillation, Ventricular Tachydysrhythmias)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Hypertension in Childhood.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use age-/sex-/height-specific blood pressure percentiles to diagnose pediatric hypertension, and recognize that a secondary cause (renal parenchymal/renovascular disease, coarctation, endocrine) is more likely the younger the child and the more severe the hypertension.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Sleep-Related Hypoventilation Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sleep-related hypoventilation due to obesity, medications, neuromuscular, chest-wall, neurologic, or severe lung disease.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sinusitis reasoning for Sinusitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose acute bacterial vs. viral rhinosinusitis using duration/severity criteria and initiate appropriate management, avoiding unnecessary antibiotics.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Coarctation of the Aorta.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize coarctation by blood-pressure discrepancy between upper and lower extremities (brachial-femoral delay, >20 mmHg difference raising suspicion), its association with bicuspid aortic valve and Turner syndrome, and that severe neonatal presentation is a ductal-dependent emergency requiring prostaglandin E1 to keep the ductus open.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply psychosis organic screen reasoning for Acute Psychosis (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Screen for organic/secondary causes of new-onset psychosis (delirium, substance-induced, autoimmune encephalitis) before attributing to primary psychiatric illness.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Vaginal Discharge and Vulvovaginitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish physiologic discharge from infectious vulvovaginitis (e.g., candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis) and from STI causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply clinical integration reasoning for Basic Pulmonary Function Test Interpretation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Relate a basic PFT pattern to the presenting respiratory syndrome and decide when further testing or referral is needed.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply edh recognition reasoning for Epidural (Extradural) Hematoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the lucid-interval presentation and biconvex/lentiform CT appearance of epidural hematoma as a neurosurgical emergency.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cervical radiculopathy reasoning for Extradural Lesions: Root Compression and Cervical Disc Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dermatomal/myotomal patterns of cervical nerve root compression and distinguish urgent (myelopathy) from non-urgent presentations.
candidates.study_unit: Extradural Lesions: Root Compression and Cervical Disc Syndrome

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Anemia of Chronic Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize anemia of chronic disease/inflammation (elevated ferritin, low TIBC, hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration) in a patient with an underlying chronic inflammatory, infectious, or malignant condition and distinguish it from iron deficiency.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pathogen by age reasoning for Pneumonia (Pediatric, Infectious Diseases Chapter -- Pathogens by Age).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select empiric antibiotic therapy for community-acquired pneumonia based on age-specific likely pathogens (e.g. GBS/E. coli in neonates, S. pneumoniae/viral across childhood, atypical organisms in school-age children) as summarized in the age-stratified treatment table.
candidates.study_unit: Pneumonia (Pediatric, Infectious Diseases Chapter -- Pathogens by Age)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Adenomyosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize adenomyosis as a cause of heavy menstrual bleeding and secondary dysmenorrhea, typically in a parous patient with a diffusely enlarged, tender uterus, and distinguish it from fibroids and endometriosis on clinical grounds.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Dissociative Amnesia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dissociative amnesia (inability to recall important autobiographical information, usually traumatic/stressful, inconsistent with ordinary forgetting) and the importance of excluding organic causes of amnesia (e.g., substance, head injury, neurocognitive disorder) first.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply obesity management reasoning for Obesity.
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess a patient with obesity for root causes/complications and collaborate on a values-based primary-care management plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Clavicle Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize clavicle fracture clinically and on x-ray, assess for neurovascular (brachial plexus/subclavian vessel) compromise, and know non-operative sling management is standard for most mid-shaft fractures.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply xanthoma workup reasoning for Lipoma and Xanthoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize xanthoma variants as potential cutaneous markers of dyslipidemia or hematologic disease and order a fasting lipid panel accordingly.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply postpartum counselling reasoning for Postpartum Care (Routine Care, Breastfeeding and Medication Safety).
candidates.source_competency_text: Provide routine postpartum care and counsel on medication safety during breastfeeding.
candidates.study_unit: Postpartum Care (Routine Care, Breastfeeding and Medication Safety)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply occupational history reasoning for Occupational Medicine Overview and Occupational History Taking.
candidates.source_competency_text: Take a structured occupational history (current/previous duties, exposure identification and assessment, temporal relationship to symptoms, co-worker symptoms, non-work exposures) to determine whether a presenting condition is work-related.
candidates.study_unit: Occupational Medicine Overview and Occupational History Taking

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pathogens reasoning for Gastroenteritis (Pediatric, Infectious Diseases Chapter -- Pathogens).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize common viral (rotavirus, norovirus) vs. bacterial (Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, E. coli) causes of pediatric gastroenteritis and features suggesting a bacterial etiology (bloody diarrhea, high fever, severe abdominal pain).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply economic evaluation types reasoning for Economic Evaluation of Health Interventions (CEA, CUA, CBA).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish cost-effectiveness analysis (natural health-outcome units), cost-utility analysis (QALY-based), and cost-benefit analysis (all outcomes monetized), and calculate/interpret an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER).
candidates.study_unit: Economic Evaluation of Health Interventions (CEA, CUA, CBA)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply induction decision reasoning for Induction of Labour (Indications and Methods).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications/contraindications for labour induction and outline the major methods (mechanical, prostaglandin, oxytocin).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Vaginal Cancer.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize abnormal vaginal bleeding or a visible vaginal lesion in an at-risk patient (e.g., prior cervical dysplasia, DES exposure) as a rare but important cause requiring biopsy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply scabies recognition reasoning for Parasitic and Arthropod Skin Infestations (Scabies, Lice, Bed Bugs, Cutaneous Larva Migrans, Leishmaniasis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize scabies by nocturnal pruritus, burrows in web spaces/flexures, and treat the patient plus close contacts with permethrin.
candidates.study_unit: Parasitic and Arthropod Skin Infestations (Scabies, Lice, Bed Bugs, Cutaneous Larva Migrans, Leishmaniasis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hypopituitarism reasoning for Pituitary Pathology: Adenoma and Hypopituitarism.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply 'The Eight I's' etiology framework (including Sheehan's syndrome and pituitary apoplexy) and recognize axis-specific deficiency symptoms and the dynamic-testing approach to hypopituitarism.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply erysipelas vs cellulitis reasoning for Bacterial Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Impetigo, Erysipelas, Cellulitis, Folliculitis/Furuncle/Carbuncle, Skin Abscess).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish erysipelas (sharp raised border, upper dermis/lymphatics) from cellulitis (poorly demarcated, lower dermis/subcutaneous fat) and select first-line antibiotics.
candidates.study_unit: Bacterial Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Impetigo, Erysipelas, Cellulitis, Folliculitis/Furuncle/Carbuncle, Skin Abscess)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Cellulitis, Necrotizing Fasciitis, Acquired Oral Lesions).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize cellulitis and distinguish it from the surgical emergency of necrotizing fasciitis based on clinical red flags (pain out of proportion, rapid progression, systemic toxicity).
candidates.study_unit: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Cellulitis, Necrotizing Fasciitis, Acquired Oral Lesions)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize BPD as chronic oxygen/ventilator-dependent lung disease of prematurity (defined by oxygen requirement at 36 wk corrected gestational age) and its long-term respiratory implications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ethical reasoning reasoning for Reproductive Technologies.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply informed consent principles to reproductive technology decisions (e.g., IVF, surrogacy, gamete donation).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Patellar Dislocation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize lateral patellar dislocation (positive apprehension test, often self-reducing) in the classic young-female demographic, and know most first-time dislocations are managed non-operatively with closed reduction.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency contraception reasoning for Contraception.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications and time-sensitive window for emergency postcoital contraception.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Tinnitus (DDx, Definition, History, Investigations, Management).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize unilateral, pulsatile, or objective tinnitus (audible to the examiner) as requiring further workup (vascular imaging or MRI for acoustic neuroma) rather than routine reassurance, and distinguish subjective (patient-only) tinnitus associated with SNHL from vascular/mechanical causes of objective tinnitus.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Aphasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a patient with a language deficit, distinguish aphasia (language) from dysarthria (speech), classify by fluency/comprehension/repetition (e.g., Broca's vs. Wernicke's), and localize to the dominant hemisphere.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply chest pain ddx reasoning for Chest Pain (ED Approach, incl. Life-Threatening ECG Changes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate life-threatening (ACS, PE, aortic dissection, tamponade, tension pneumothorax) from benign causes of chest pain.
candidates.study_unit: Chest Pain (ED Approach, incl. Life-Threatening ECG Changes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigate reasoning for Approach to joint pain and patterns of joint involvement.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use number and pattern of joints to focus the initial differential.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to joint pain and patterns of joint involvement

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cholangitis recognition reasoning for Ascending Cholangitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Charcot's triad/Reynolds' pentad as suggestive of ascending cholangitis, a biliary emergency requiring urgent biliary decompression and antibiotics.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Myocarditis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize myocarditis presentation (often post-viral, chest pain/dyspnea with elevated troponin and normal coronaries).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply agent selection reasoning for Induction Technique and Agents.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select an induction agent appropriate to patient comorbidity (e.g., avoid propofol/thiopental in fixed cardiac output or shock; avoid ketamine in psychosis or uncontrolled HTN; favor etomidate in hemodynamic instability).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Urinary Incontinence.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose common incontinence patterns and initiate initial management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply anaphylaxis mgmt reasoning for Anaphylaxis and Allergic Reactions.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize anaphylaxis and initiate immediate epinephrine-first management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Laryngomalacia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize inspiratory stridor worsening with feeding/supine positioning and improving prone in an otherwise well infant as laryngomalacia, and know most cases resolve spontaneously by 12-18 mo with surgery (supraglottoplasty) reserved for severe cases (failure to thrive, apnea).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pharyngitis reasoning for Sore Throat (Pharyngitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause of sore throat/pharyngitis, apply criteria (e.g., Centor score) to identify likely streptococcal pharyngitis, and initiate appropriate management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish dry from wet (neovascular) AMD, recognize acute metamorphopsia/central scotoma in known AMD as a wet-conversion red flag requiring urgent referral for anti-VEGF therapy, and counsel on Amsler-grid self-monitoring.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply manage reasoning for Ankylosing spondylitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Arrange appropriate investigation and rheumatology referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply iugr management reasoning for Intrauterine Growth Restriction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify modifiable risk factors for IUGR, apply routine fetal growth monitoring, and recognize the need for specialized surveillance/referral and delivery-timing decisions.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply efm interpretation reasoning for Fetal Monitoring in Labour.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret intrapartum fetal heart rate monitoring (baseline, variability, accelerations, decelerations) and apply the corresponding category-based management response.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply medical surveillance reasoning for Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify an appropriate secondary-prevention medical surveillance test for a given occupational exposure (e.g., audiograms for noise, spirometry for dust exposure, blood lead testing for lead exposure).
candidates.study_unit: Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention

candidates.principal_decision: Apply counselling reasoning for Gender-Affirming Surgery.
candidates.source_competency_text: Provide respectful, informed counselling to a transgender patient about the existence of gender-affirming surgical options and the referral pathway, without needing procedure-level technical knowledge.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Pediatric Meningitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize age-specific meningitis presentations (nonspecific in neonates: poor feeding, lethargy, temperature instability; classic triad of fever/neck stiffness/altered mental status more reliable in older children) and the urgency of empiric antibiotics +/- LP without delaying treatment for imaging when there are no contraindications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Dyspnea (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dyspnea presentations requiring urgent assessment (ABCs).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply osteoporosis screening reasoning for Osteoporosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply DEXA-based diagnostic criteria (T-score) and fracture risk assessment tools to screen for and diagnose osteoporosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Sleep Apnea.
candidates.source_competency_text: Choose appropriate sleep testing and interpret a basic diagnostic result at a generalist level.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Major Neurocognitive Disorder / Dementia (Overview, Alzheimer's, Lewy Body, Frontotemporal, and Vascular Subtypes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a patient with progressive cognitive decline, distinguish dementia from delirium/depression, and differentiate Alzheimer's, Lewy body, frontotemporal, and vascular dementia by their distinguishing clinical features (e.g., early visual hallucinations/parkinsonism in DLB, early personality/behavioural change in FTD, stepwise decline in vascular dementia), and screen for reversible causes.
candidates.study_unit: Major Neurocognitive Disorder / Dementia (Overview, Alzheimer's, Lewy Body, Frontotemporal, and Vascular Subtypes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply meningioma recognition reasoning for Meningioma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize meningioma as the most common benign extra-axial primary brain tumour and its typical presentation/imaging appearance.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply definitions reasoning for Concepts of Health, Health Equity, and Cultural Safety.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish disease, illness, sickness, impairment, disability, and handicap, and health equity from health equality.
candidates.study_unit: Concepts of Health, Health Equity, and Cultural Safety

candidates.principal_decision: Apply half life reasoning for Pharmacokinetic Parameters and Dosing Strategy (Half-Life, Clearance, Steady-State, Loading/Maintenance Dosing).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the concept of elimination half-life to predict time to steady state (4-5 half-lives) and time to complete elimination after stopping a drug.
candidates.study_unit: Pharmacokinetic Parameters and Dosing Strategy (Half-Life, Clearance, Steady-State, Loading/Maintenance Dosing)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Herpes Simplex Keratitis and Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dendritic corneal ulceration (HSV keratitis, topical corticosteroids contraindicated) and Hutchinson's sign (nasociliary nerve involvement predicting ocular herpes zoster) as requiring urgent ophthalmology referral.
candidates.study_unit: Herpes Simplex Keratitis and Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus

candidates.principal_decision: Apply return to work reasoning for Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the restrictions/limitations/abilities/tolerance framework to a tertiary-prevention return-to-work planning scenario.
candidates.study_unit: Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention

candidates.principal_decision: Apply liver neoplasm recognition reasoning for Liver Neoplasms (Surgical).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish benign (hemangioma, focal nodular hyperplasia, adenoma) from malignant (hepatocellular carcinoma, metastatic) liver lesions and identify appropriate initial workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply system navigation reasoning for Clinical Informatics and Digital Health Ethics.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use health information systems safely, recognizing their limitations.
candidates.study_unit: Clinical Informatics and Digital Health Ethics

candidates.principal_decision: Apply splenic trauma management reasoning for Splenic Trauma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize splenic injury on trauma imaging/FAST exam, grade severity, and identify indications for nonoperative vs. operative (splenectomy) management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply scc bowens recognition reasoning for Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers (Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Bowen's Disease).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) and invasive SCC, and understand their progression risk and management (excision, electrodesiccation).
candidates.study_unit: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers (Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Bowen's Disease)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply exposure history reasoning for Pneumoconioses and Occupational Fibrotic Lung Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Take a specific occupational and environmental exposure history for asbestos, silica, coal, and related hazards.
candidates.study_unit: Pneumoconioses and Occupational Fibrotic Lung Disease

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Chest Pain (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate cardiac (ACS, pericarditis, aortic dissection) from noncardiac (GI, musculoskeletal, pulmonary, psychiatric) causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply benign breast recognition reasoning for Benign Breast Lesions.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish benign breast lesions (fibroadenoma, fibrocystic change, mastitis) from features requiring biopsy to exclude malignancy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply overdose approach reasoning for Approach to the Overdose/Poisoned Patient (History, Primary/Secondary Survey, Universal Antidotes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply a systematic primary/secondary survey approach (ABCD3EFG) to an undifferentiated overdose/poisoning presentation.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to the Overdose/Poisoned Patient (History, Primary/Secondary Survey, Universal Antidotes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sample size effects reasoning for Population, Sampling Methods, and Sample Size.
candidates.source_competency_text: Explain that increasing sample size improves precision (narrower CIs) and reduces Type I/II error probability, but does not reduce bias or confounding.
candidates.study_unit: Population, Sampling Methods, and Sample Size

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Dysmenorrhea.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate primary from secondary dysmenorrhea and recognize secondary causes (e.g., endometriosis, adenomyosis, fibroids) requiring further workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hg management reasoning for Hyperemesis Gravidarum.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hyperemesis gravidarum, assess severity/complications (dehydration, ketonuria, weight loss), and initiate management including antiemetics and admission criteria.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Loss of Vision (Differential Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish sudden painless (vascular/retinal emergency), sudden painful, and gradual/progressive vision loss, and identify which require same-day ophthalmology referral versus urgent stroke workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply response framework reasoning for Disaster Preparedness, Emergency Response, and Recovery.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery as sequential phases of disaster management, and identify the role of an Emergency Response Plan, Incident Management System, Emergency Operations Centre, and Continuity of Operations Plan.
candidates.study_unit: Disaster Preparedness, Emergency Response, and Recovery

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Burn Injury Classification, Pathophysiology, and Severity Assessment.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the zone-of-injury model (hyperemia, stasis, coagulation) as it relates to burn progression and resuscitation urgency.
candidates.study_unit: Burn Injury Classification, Pathophysiology, and Severity Assessment

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Vomiting (Pediatric, Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish bilious from non-bilious vomiting (bilious vomiting in a neonate/infant is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise -- malrotation with volvulus) and recognize non-GI causes (raised ICP, metabolic disease, UTI, pyloric stenosis).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Childhood Absence Epilepsy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize childhood absence epilepsy (brief staring/behavioural-arrest spells without postictal confusion, provoked by hyperventilation, classic 3 Hz generalized spike-and-wave EEG) and its generally good prognosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Lymphoma (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish Hodgkin from non-Hodgkin lymphoma by typical age/presentation (Hodgkin: painless cervical/mediastinal adenopathy, B symptoms, bimodal-ish adolescent peak; NHL: more rapidly progressive, extranodal involvement common) as a cause within the lymphadenopathy differential.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Transient Synovitis of the Hip.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish transient synovitis (well-appearing, low-grade or no fever, able to bear some weight, normal/mildly elevated inflammatory markers, self-limited) from septic arthritis using the Kocher criteria.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Pancytopenia (Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Generate a differential for pancytopenia (bone marrow failure/infiltration, peripheral destruction, sequestration) and identify features requiring urgent bone marrow evaluation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply molluscum recognition reasoning for Molluscum Contagiosum and Cutaneous HPV (Warts).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize molluscum contagiosum as a self-limited viral infection and select observation vs. destructive therapy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply refractory symptoms reasoning for Suffering: Definition, Sources, and Relief of Refractory Physical/Existential Suffering.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize palliative sedation therapy as an option reserved for intolerable, refractory physical symptoms in the final hours of life, requiring specialist palliative care consultation.
candidates.study_unit: Suffering: Definition, Sources, and Relief of Refractory Physical/Existential Suffering

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Parkinson's Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the cardinal features of Parkinson's disease (bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, postural instability), differentiate from other parkinsonian syndromes, and outline the initial management approach.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Bereavement (Normal and Complicated Grief).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish normal grief from complicated/prolonged grief or superimposed major depressive disorder, and recognize when grief therapy alone vs. added pharmacotherapy is indicated (comorbid MDD, past mood-disorder history, or severe symptoms).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Foreign Body (Airway/Aerodigestive Tract).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sudden-onset choking, unilateral wheeze, or asymmetric breath sounds in a toddler as suspicious for an inhaled foreign body, and know rigid bronchoscopy (not blind finger sweeps) is the definitive management for a witnessed or strongly suspected airway foreign body.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Macrocytic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize neurologic manifestations specific to B12 (not folate) deficiency and the risk of precipitating/worsening them with unrecognized folate-only replacement.
candidates.study_unit: Macrocytic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency

candidates.principal_decision: Apply fatigue reasoning for Fatigue.
candidates.source_competency_text: Perform a thorough primary-care history and physical examination to establish an underlying cause of fatigue.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dili recognition reasoning for Drug-Induced Liver Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize medication/toxin exposure (including acetaminophen overdose) as a cause of acute or chronic liver injury and initiate appropriate management (e.g., N-acetylcysteine for acetaminophen toxicity).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Cardiac Tumours.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize atrial myxoma as a rare cause of positional syncope, embolic events, or constitutional symptoms with a mobile mass on echocardiography.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognize reasoning for Osteoarthritis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the typical mechanical presentation and radiographic features.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Bone and Soft Tissue Tumours: Aggressive vs. Non-Aggressive Lesion Recognition.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish aggressive from non-aggressive bone lesions on x-ray using periosteal reaction pattern (Codman's triangle/onion skin/sunburst vs. benign remodeling), zone of transition, and presence of a soft tissue mass, to determine urgency of biopsy/referral.
candidates.study_unit: Bone and Soft Tissue Tumours: Aggressive vs. Non-Aggressive Lesion Recognition

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pattern recognition reasoning for Basic Chest Radiograph Patterns.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize basic consolidation, interstitial, nodular, pleural, hyperinflation, and collapse patterns on a chest radiograph.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply testing reasoning for HIV Testing, Pre/Post-Test Counselling, and Prevention (PrEP/PEP).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate nominal, non-nominal, and anonymous HIV testing pathways and their Public Health notification obligations.
candidates.study_unit: HIV Testing, Pre/Post-Test Counselling, and Prevention (PrEP/PEP)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply insulin regimen selection reasoning for Treatment of Diabetes: Glycemic Targets, Lifestyle, and Pharmacotherapy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select and titrate basal, basal-bolus, or premixed insulin regimens for T1DM and T2DM, and apply sick-day medication-holding rules (SADMANS).
candidates.study_unit: Treatment of Diabetes: Glycemic Targets, Lifestyle, and Pharmacotherapy

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hyperhidrosis recognition reasoning for Nail Disorders and Primary Hyperhidrosis (Adnexal Disorders).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize primary hyperhidrosis by focal, bilateral, waking-hours sweating without an underlying cause and select first-line management (antiperspirants, botulinum toxin).
candidates.study_unit: Nail Disorders and Primary Hyperhidrosis (Adnexal Disorders)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ethical reasoning reasoning for Resource Allocation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply principles of equitable and ethical resource allocation in a scenario of scarcity.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply legal professional action reasoning for Consent and Capacity.
candidates.source_competency_text: Determine the appropriate consent process, including for incapable patients (substitute decision-maker).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Gynecological Imaging (Transabdominal/Transvaginal Ultrasound, Hysterosalpingogram, Sonohysterogram).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select transvaginal ultrasound as first-line imaging for suspected ectopic pregnancy or early pregnancy complications, and recognize hysterosalpingogram as the investigation of choice for tubal-patency assessment in infertility workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Urothelial and Bladder Carcinoma Recognition.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify hematuria patterns requiring malignancy evaluation and referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Aplastic Anemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the need for urgent hematology referral and supportive care (transfusion, infection prophylaxis) pending transplant/immunosuppressive therapy evaluation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Congenital Hand Anomalies.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize major categories of congenital hand anomaly (syndactyly, polydactyly, radial club hand, constriction band syndrome) as findings warranting pediatric/hand-surgery referral, without requiring detailed ASSH sub-classification.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ptl management reasoning for Preterm Labour.
candidates.source_competency_text: Investigate the cause of preterm labour, assess maternal/fetal risk, and initiate management including identification of patients requiring transfer to a centre with neonatal intensive care.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Mediastinal Abnormalities and Cardiac Silhouette (Mediastinal Mass Compartments, Cardiomegaly).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize cardiomegaly on chest imaging using the cardiothoracic ratio.
candidates.study_unit: Mediastinal Abnormalities and Cardiac Silhouette (Mediastinal Mass Compartments, Cardiomegaly)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prognosis management reasoning for Schizoaffective Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize an intermediate prognosis between schizophrenia and mood disorder, and that management combines antipsychotics with mood stabilizers/antidepressants as indicated.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hzv recognition reasoning for Herpes Simplex Virus and Herpes Zoster Virus Infections.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize herpes zoster by unilateral dermatomal vesicular eruption, identify Hutchinson's sign as indicating ocular involvement requiring urgent ophthalmology referral, and initiate antivirals within 72 hours.
candidates.study_unit: Herpes Simplex Virus and Herpes Zoster Virus Infections

candidates.principal_decision: Apply safety monitoring reasoning for Mood Disorders in Children and Adolescents.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the need for close follow-up when starting SSRIs in adolescents to monitor for increased suicidal ideation/behaviour.
candidates.study_unit: Mood Disorders in Children and Adolescents

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize ARDS from acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, bilateral opacities, and a noncardiogenic context.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sjs ten management reasoning for Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN).
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate immediate drug discontinuation and refer to an ICU/burn unit for supportive care; recognize high-risk causative drugs (allopurinol, anti-epileptics, sulfonamides) and associated HLA alleles.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Ocular Pain (Differential Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Localize pain (surface/foreign-body-type vs. deep/boring) to narrow the differential and identify red-flag features requiring urgent referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Infertility and Andrology.
candidates.source_competency_text: Undertake initial couple-level infertility assessment and arrange appropriate investigation/referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sepsis recognition reasoning for Sepsis and Septic Shock (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply SIRS/qSOFA criteria to recognize sepsis and septic shock and initiate early source control and resuscitation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognize reasoning for Gout.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize acute gout and distinguish it from septic arthritis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency recognition reasoning for Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize AML presenting with pancytopenia symptoms (fatigue, infection, bleeding) +/- blasts on peripheral smear as a hematologic emergency requiring urgent hematology referral and bone marrow biopsy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Sleep Disturbances.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish common behavioural pediatric sleep disturbances (night terrors, sleepwalking, behavioural insomnia) from pathologic causes (obstructive sleep apnea) warranting further workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply urgency reasoning for Pelvic Mass.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize features indicating need for immediate investigation or referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dysuria reasoning for Dysuria.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause of dysuria (most commonly uncomplicated cystitis) in a primary-care patient and initiate appropriate empiric management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach selection reasoning for Qualitative vs. Quantitative Research Approaches.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish qualitative from quantitative research approaches by their typical research questions, sampling logic, and data type, and recognize PICO as a quantitative question-formulation framework.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Metatarsal Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish a 5th metatarsal avulsion fracture (conservative management) from a Jones fracture (proximal shaft, higher nonunion risk, may need surgical fixation), and apply the Ottawa Foot Rules to guide imaging.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Nuclear Medicine Abdominal and Genitourinary Imaging (HIDA Scan, RBC Scan for GI Bleed, Urea Breath Test, Functional Renal Imaging).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize HIDA scan as the confirmatory study for acute cholecystitis when abdominal ultrasound is equivocal, and the urea breath test as the preferred non-invasive method to diagnose and confirm eradication of active H. pylori infection.
candidates.study_unit: Nuclear Medicine Abdominal and Genitourinary Imaging (HIDA Scan, RBC Scan for GI Bleed, Urea Breath Test, Functional Renal Imaging)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bp diagnosis reasoning for Bullous Pemphigoid.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize bullous pemphigoid by tense subepidermal bullae in an elderly patient and immunofluorescence showing linear IgG/C3 at the basement membrane.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bad news reasoning for Communication in Palliative Care (incl. SPIKES Protocol for Breaking Bad News).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the SPIKES protocol (Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy/Summary) to structure a bad-news or prognosis-disclosure conversation.
candidates.study_unit: Communication in Palliative Care (incl. SPIKES Protocol for Breaking Bad News)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply levels of evidence reasoning for Critical Appraisal and Levels of Evidence.
candidates.source_competency_text: Rank Level I-V evidence by study design (RCT/meta-analysis down to expert opinion) and recognize that classification reflects the nature, not automatically the credibility, of the evidence.
candidates.study_unit: Critical Appraisal and Levels of Evidence

candidates.principal_decision: Apply smoking cessation reasoning for Smoking Cessation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Counsel a patient on smoking cessation and select appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy (NRT, varenicline, or bupropion).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognize reasoning for Sjögren syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sicca symptoms with systemic features and the need for appropriate assessment or referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Benign Active and Aggressive Bone Tumours.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize benign bone lesion features (well-defined margins, cortex intact, no periosteal reaction) and know most benign active/aggressive lesions require observation or simple curettage rather than oncologic workup.
candidates.study_unit: Benign Active and Aggressive Bone Tumours

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Enuresis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish primary from secondary and monosymptomatic from non-monosymptomatic enuresis, and recognize red flags (daytime symptoms, UTI, polyuria/polydipsia, neurologic signs) that warrant investigation for an underlying medical cause rather than reassurance alone.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply motor disorder recognition reasoning for Esophageal Motor Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize achalasia and diffuse esophageal spasm as neuromuscular causes of esophageal dysphagia and select appropriate initial investigation (e.g., manometry, barium swallow).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply morphology to ddx reasoning for Approach to Skin Lesions: Morphology, Distribution, and Differential Diagnosis of Common Presentations.
candidates.source_competency_text: Generate a limited differential diagnosis for a described lesion morphology (e.g., vesicle, bulla, pustule, oral ulcer) using infectious, inflammatory, drug/toxin, and miscellaneous categories.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to Skin Lesions: Morphology, Distribution, and Differential Diagnosis of Common Presentations

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pud diagnosis reasoning for Peptic Ulcer Disease (H. pylori, NSAID-, and Stress-Induced).
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose peptic ulcer disease, determine H. pylori vs. NSAID vs. stress-related etiology, and initiate an appropriate management plan including H. pylori eradication and PPI prophylaxis where indicated.
candidates.study_unit: Peptic Ulcer Disease (H. pylori, NSAID-, and Stress-Induced)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Motor Delay.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize motor-milestone red flags (not sitting by 9 mo, not walking by 18 mo) warranting further neurologic/developmental workup, distinguishing isolated motor delay from global developmental delay.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply postop resp complications reasoning for Postoperative Respiratory Complications (Dyspnea, Atelectasis, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize and initiate management of postoperative dyspnea, atelectasis, pneumonia, and pulmonary embolism, and identify patients requiring urgent escalation.
candidates.study_unit: Postoperative Respiratory Complications (Dyspnea, Atelectasis, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply structure reasoning for Public Health Context: Definitions and Structure of Public Health in Canada.
candidates.source_competency_text: Describe the federal/provincial/municipal structure of the Canadian public health system, PHAC's mission and core public health functions, and how public health and preventive medicine as a specialty differs from clinical medicine.
candidates.study_unit: Public Health Context: Definitions and Structure of Public Health in Canada

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Generalized Edema.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate cardiac (heart failure) from renal, hepatic, and other systemic causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply routine care reasoning for Routine Neonatal Care.
candidates.source_competency_text: Outline routine newborn care after delivery (vitamin K administration, ocular antimicrobial prophylaxis, newborn metabolic/hearing screening, physical exam for congenital anomalies) and standard discharge criteria.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply other dm complications reasoning for Other Complications of Diabetes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize additional diabetes-associated complications (diabetic foot, gastroparesis, increased infection risk) requiring surveillance.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Floaters.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sudden shower of floaters +/- flashes/curtain field loss as requiring urgent same-day ophthalmology assessment to rule out retinal detachment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply significance reasoning for Statistical Hypothesis Testing, Error Types, and Confidence Intervals.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish statistical significance (p<0.05, unlikely due to chance) from clinical significance (magnitude of benefit that matters to a patient).
candidates.study_unit: Statistical Hypothesis Testing, Error Types, and Confidence Intervals

candidates.principal_decision: Apply modality matching reasoning for Psychotherapeutic Modalities Overview.
candidates.source_competency_text: Match common psychotherapy modalities (supportive therapy, IPT, CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing, group therapy, family therapy, mindfulness-based therapies, psychodynamic therapy) to their primary indications (e.g., DBT for borderline personality disorder and self-harm; motivational interviewing for substance use; CBT as first-line for most mood/anxiety/OCD presentations) at a recognition level, without needing technique-level protocol detail.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply terminology reasoning for Outbreak, Epidemic, and Pandemic Definitions and Measures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish outbreak, endemic, epidemic, and pandemic by scale and expected baseline frequency.
candidates.study_unit: Outbreak, Epidemic, and Pandemic Definitions and Measures

candidates.principal_decision: Apply adolescent interview reasoning for Adolescent Medicine (HEEADSSS Interview, Confidentiality, Adolescent Consent).
candidates.source_competency_text: Conduct an adolescent-appropriate psychosocial interview (HEEADSSS/SSHADESS) with attention to confidentiality limits and mature-minor consent principles specific to adolescent care.
candidates.study_unit: Adolescent Medicine (HEEADSSS Interview, Confidentiality, Adolescent Consent)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply design identification reasoning for Observational Study Designs (Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional, Ecological).
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a study description, identify whether it is an ecological, cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort design.
candidates.study_unit: Observational Study Designs (Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional, Ecological)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply an age-specific pediatric LGIB differential (anal fissure in infants, intussusception with 'currant jelly' stool, Meckel diverticulum with painless bleeding, juvenile polyp, IBD in older children).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Substance Use Disorders: General Approach and Diagnosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply DSM-5 substance use disorder criteria (mild 2-3, moderate 4-5, severe >=6 of 11 criteria within 12 mo) uniformly across substances.
candidates.study_unit: Substance Use Disorders: General Approach and Diagnosis

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Thalassemia (Alpha and Beta, Minor/Major/Intermedia).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the transfusion/chelation-dependence spectrum and genetic counselling indication.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply exam reasoning for Cervical Spine (Approach, Red Flags, Imaging).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply cervical spine special tests (compression, distraction, Spurling) to localize radiculopathy vs. myelopathy, and recognize which neck-pain presentations require acute-trauma imaging/Neurosurgery involvement.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Necrotizing Fasciitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize red-flag features of necrotizing fasciitis (pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading erythema, crepitus, systemic toxicity) and initiate emergent surgical consultation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply growth monitoring reasoning for Growth and Development (Growth Charts, Growth Velocity, Developmental Milestones).
candidates.source_competency_text: Use WHO growth charts (and the Fenton curve, corrected for gestational age until 2 yr, in former preterm infants) to distinguish normal growth velocity from growth faltering.
candidates.study_unit: Growth and Development (Growth Charts, Growth Velocity, Developmental Milestones)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cord prolapse management reasoning for Umbilical Cord Prolapse.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize umbilical cord prolapse and initiate emergency management (manual elevation of the presenting part, positioning, emergent delivery).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Cellulitis, Necrotizing Fasciitis, Acquired Oral Lesions).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate oral candidiasis from oral squamous cell carcinoma based on risk factors and morphology.
candidates.study_unit: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Cellulitis, Necrotizing Fasciitis, Acquired Oral Lesions)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply environmental racism recognition reasoning for Environmental Racism (Grassy Narrows and Africville).
candidates.source_competency_text: Define environmental racism and recognize Grassy Narrows (Indigenous, mercury contamination) and Africville (Black community, industrial siting and forced relocation) as the chapter's named Canadian examples.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prediction reasoning for Difficult Airway: Recognition and Initial Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify preoperative predictors of a difficult airway from history and airway exam.
candidates.study_unit: Difficult Airway: Recognition and Initial Management

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Erysipelas and Cellulitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate erysipelas from cellulitis by depth/margin characteristics and identify risk factors (PVD, DM, lymphedema, portal of entry).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dizziness reasoning for Dizziness.
candidates.source_competency_text: Discriminate vertigo from other causes of dizziness in a primary-care patient and initiate an appropriate management/referral plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply normal staging reasoning for Stages of Puberty.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the normal sequence and timing of pubertal stages (Tanner staging, menarche timing) as the baseline for identifying precocious or delayed puberty.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Infectious Pediatric Exanthems (Differential Diagnosis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate common infectious pediatric exanthems by rash distribution/timing, associated features, and incubation/communicability (e.g. measles' 3 Cs and Koplik spots with cephalocaudal spread vs. erythema infectiosum's 'slapped cheek' appearance vs. hand-foot-mouth's posterior-oral enanthem), and recognize measles as a reportable, vaccine-preventable disease requiring airborne isolation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention reasoning for Respiratory Infections (Pneumonia).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recommend influenza/pneumococcal vaccination per Public Health Agency of Canada guidance to reduce pneumonia risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Hand Tendon Injuries (Flexor and Extensor).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize clinical signs of flexor vs. extensor tendon injury (loss of active flexion/extension at the relevant joint) and understand the greater urgency of flexor tendon repair due to retraction risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply tool selection reasoning for Palliative Care Assessment Tools (ESAS, Palliative Performance Scale).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish the purpose of the ESAS (patient-reported symptom-intensity screening across 9-10 domains) from the PPS (clinician-rated functional status with prognostic value, read by dropping down the ambulation column).
candidates.study_unit: Palliative Care Assessment Tools (ESAS, Palliative Performance Scale)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply first pass reasoning for Pharmacokinetics Overview and Drug Absorption.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the concept of first-pass metabolism to explain why oral bioavailability differs from IV bioavailability (F=1) and why some routes (sublingual, rectal, transdermal) are chosen specifically to reduce first-pass exposure.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Binge-Eating Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose binge-eating disorder (recurrent binge eating episodes with marked distress, at least weekly for 3 mo, without regular compensatory behaviour) and distinguish from bulimia nervosa by the absence of compensatory behaviour.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Huntington's Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize chorea with autosomal dominant family history and psychiatric/cognitive decline as suggestive of Huntington's disease, and understand the basis for genetic counselling/testing.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Lacrimal Apparatus Disorders (Dry Eye, Epiphora, Dacryocystitis, Dacryoadenitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dacryocystitis (acute lacrimal-sac infection) as requiring antibiotic treatment and possible urgent referral, and distinguish it from the chronic, low-acuity dry-eye/epiphora spectrum.
candidates.study_unit: Lacrimal Apparatus Disorders (Dry Eye, Epiphora, Dacryocystitis, Dacryoadenitis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Chest Pain (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select initial investigations (ECG, troponin, CXR) appropriate to clinical probability.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Osteomyelitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize fever, bone pain, and elevated inflammatory markers as osteomyelitis requiring blood cultures, imaging, and urgent orthopedic/infectious diseases involvement.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply aneurysm recognition reasoning for Intracranial Aneurysms.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize intracranial aneurysm as the cause of SAH and the basic surgical/endovascular options (clipping vs. coiling) without requiring technique-level detail.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Pulmonary Vascular Abnormalities: Pulmonary Edema and Pulmonary Embolism Imaging.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the CXR and CT findings of pulmonary edema and their correlation with cardiogenic vs. non-cardiogenic etiology.
candidates.study_unit: Pulmonary Vascular Abnormalities: Pulmonary Edema and Pulmonary Embolism Imaging

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis and management reasoning for Iron Deficiency Anemia (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize iron deficiency anemia risk factors (excess cow's milk >24 oz/d, prematurity, delayed complementary feeding) and first-line management (oral iron supplementation, dietary counselling).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hydrocephalus classification reasoning for Hydrocephalus.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate obstructive vs. non-obstructive hydrocephalus and recognize NPH's classic triad.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply epidemic curve interpretation reasoning for Steps to Control an Outbreak and Epidemic Curves.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret an epidemic curve to distinguish a point-source, continuous-source, or propagated-source outbreak.
candidates.study_unit: Steps to Control an Outbreak and Epidemic Curves

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Popliteal Cysts (Baker's Cyst).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize a popliteal (Baker's) cyst as usually benign, associated with underlying knee pathology (meniscal tear, OA) in adults, and distinguish it from DVT if it ruptures (pseudothrombophlebitis).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply system navigation reasoning for Canadian Healthcare System: Structure, Funding, and Delivery.
candidates.source_competency_text: Describe the basic structure, funding model (public single-payer for medically necessary services), and delivery mechanisms of the Canadian healthcare system.
candidates.study_unit: Canadian Healthcare System: Structure, Funding, and Delivery

candidates.principal_decision: Apply twin pregnancy management reasoning for Multi-Fetal Gestation (Twin Pregnancy) including Twin-Twin Transfusion Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Determine chorionicity and apply the corresponding surveillance intensity, and recognize twin-twin transfusion syndrome as a monochorionic-specific complication requiring specialized referral.
candidates.study_unit: Multi-Fetal Gestation (Twin Pregnancy) including Twin-Twin Transfusion Syndrome

candidates.principal_decision: Apply localization reasoning for Lesion Localization (CNS vs. PNS Localization Framework).
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a described pattern of motor, sensory, or reflex findings, classify the lesion as cortical, subcortical, brainstem, cerebellar, spinal cord, anterior horn cell, nerve root, or peripheral nerve/NMJ/muscle, and state the localizing implication (e.g., crossed findings = brainstem; sensory level = cord).
candidates.study_unit: Lesion Localization (CNS vs. PNS Localization Framework)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Temporal Bone Fractures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of basilar skull fracture (Battle's sign, raccoon eyes, CSF oto/rhinorrhea, hemotympanum) after head trauma, avoid instrumenting/syringing the ear canal, and know immediate complete facial nerve palsy after trauma is a surgical indication.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Hereditary Spherocytosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hereditary spherocytosis (hemolytic anemia, spherocytes on smear, negative DAT, splenomegaly, increased risk of pigment gallstones) and its distinction from autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hbv hcv screening reasoning for Viral Hepatitis (A, B, C, D).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications for hepatitis B and C screening and the risk of chronic infection/cirrhosis/hepatocellular carcinoma.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply jurisdiction reasoning for Legislation and Organization of Public Health in Canada.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify which level of government (federal, provincial, municipal) and which named agency is responsible for a given public health function or piece of legislation in Canada.
candidates.study_unit: Legislation and Organization of Public Health in Canada

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pheo recognition reasoning for Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma by the classic episodic triad (headache, palpitations, diaphoresis) with paroxysmal hypertension, and screen with plasma or urine fractionated metanephrines.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cyst recognition reasoning for Cysts (Epidermal, Pilar, Dermoid, Milium).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish common benign cutaneous cysts (epidermal, pilar, dermoid, milium) by clinical features and site, and recognize which require no treatment versus elective excision.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Cannabis Use Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the characteristic intoxication/withdrawal presentation and health consequences of this substance.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply risk benefit counselling reasoning for Menopause Hormone Therapy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the indications, contraindications, and major risk/benefit considerations for menopause hormone therapy at a level sufficient to counsel and initiate referral, without reference to a specific current regimen.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Infected Wounds.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize clinical signs of wound infection and initiate appropriate management (debridement, antibiotics, delayed closure).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dcm recognition reasoning for Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize progressive gait disturbance, hand clumsiness, and UMN signs in an older patient as possible degenerative cervical myelopathy requiring MRI and surgical referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply staging reasoning for Pressure Ulcers (Pressure Injuries).
candidates.source_competency_text: Stage a pressure injury and recognize prevention strategies (repositioning, offloading, skin care) and indications for surgical debridement/referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency algorithm reasoning for Difficult Airway: Recognition and Initial Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the core stepwise escalation for failed intubation/ventilation (call for help -> 100% O2 bag-mask -> LMA -> emergency surgical airway) without needing to reproduce the full published flowchart.
candidates.study_unit: Difficult Airway: Recognition and Initial Management

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Bronchiectasis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Obtain appropriate cultures and imaging, begin airway-clearance and infection management, and identify complications requiring specialist care.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply extremity injury recognition reasoning for Orthopedic (Extremity) Trauma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize limb-threatening extremity injuries (e.g. dislocation with neurovascular compromise) requiring urgent reduction.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply exposure link reasoning for Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize temporal links between inhaled occupational or hobby antigen exposure and respiratory symptoms.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pediatric considerations reasoning for Pediatric Palliative Care: Unique Considerations and Patient Categories.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that the unit of pediatric palliative care is the family (including siblings), that decision-making authority tracks the child's developmental capacity rather than chronological age, and identify the four ACT/RCPCH categories of children who may benefit from palliative care.
candidates.study_unit: Pediatric Palliative Care: Unique Considerations and Patient Categories

candidates.principal_decision: Apply esophageal perforation recognition reasoning for Esophageal Perforation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize esophageal perforation (e.g., post-endoscopic instrumentation or Boerhaave syndrome) as a surgical emergency and initiate urgent management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pediatric SLE's multisystem presentation (malar rash, photosensitivity, arthritis, nephritis, cytopenias, positive ANA) and that pediatric-onset SLE tends to be more severe than adult-onset disease.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply nnt nnh reasoning for Effectiveness of Interventions and Measures of Effect (RR, OR, AR, NNT, NNH).
candidates.source_competency_text: Calculate NNT (1/ARR) and NNH from given event rates and interpret their clinical significance, including the caution that a large relative-risk reduction can correspond to a small absolute benefit.
candidates.study_unit: Effectiveness of Interventions and Measures of Effect (RR, OR, AR, NNT, NNH)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Supraventricular Tachyarrhythmias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Determine rate vs. rhythm control strategy and anticoagulation need (CHADS-65/CHA2DS2-VASc reasoning) for atrial fibrillation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pbc recognition reasoning for Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize primary biliary cholangitis as an autoimmune cholestatic liver disease, typically in a middle-aged woman with pruritus and elevated alkaline phosphatase/AMA.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply risk assessment reasoning for HIV Infection: Epidemiology, Transmission, Natural History, and Antiretroviral Therapy Overview.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify modes of HIV transmission and per-exposure-route risk to guide counselling and post-exposure decisions.
candidates.study_unit: HIV Infection: Epidemiology, Transmission, Natural History, and Antiretroviral Therapy Overview

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Musculoskeletal Infection Imaging (Osteomyelitis, Septic Arthritis, Necrotizing Fasciitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that plain films are frequently normal early in septic arthritis and necrotizing fasciitis, and that a normal or unremarkable x-ray must never delay joint aspiration or surgical exploration when clinical suspicion is high; recognize MRI as the most sensitive modality for osteomyelitis.
candidates.study_unit: Musculoskeletal Infection Imaging (Osteomyelitis, Septic Arthritis, Necrotizing Fasciitis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sampling timing reasoning for Therapeutic Drug Monitoring.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that TDM sampling is most informative once steady-state has been reached (~4-5 half-lives).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Transient Ischemic Attack / Amaurosis Fugax.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize transient monocular vision loss (amaurosis fugax) as a TIA-equivalent requiring urgent carotid/cardiac embolic-source workup and stroke-prevention risk-factor management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pigmented lesion workup reasoning for Pigmented Nevi and Acquired Pigmented Lesions.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize when a changing or atypical pigmented lesion warrants excisional biopsy versus reassurance/photographic follow-up.
candidates.study_unit: Pigmented Nevi and Acquired Pigmented Lesions

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Retinal Vein Occlusion (Central/Branch).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize RVO (sudden painless vision loss, 'blood and thunder' fundus) and its association with hypertension, diabetes, and glaucoma, and initiate urgent ophthalmology referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply vd interpretation reasoning for Drug Distribution (Volume of Distribution, Protein Binding, Depots, Barriers).
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret a drug's volume of distribution as reflecting its tissue vs. plasma distribution pattern (small Vd -> plasma/protein-bound; large Vd -> tissue/fat depot), and apply this to explain age-related Vd changes for lipophilic drugs.
candidates.study_unit: Drug Distribution (Volume of Distribution, Protein Binding, Depots, Barriers)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply behaviour change reasoning for Health Promotion, Behaviour Change, and Community Needs Assessment.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the Health Belief Model (perceived susceptibility/severity/benefits/barriers, cues to action, self-efficacy) and the Stages of Change Model (precontemplation through maintenance) to a patient behaviour-change scenario.
candidates.study_unit: Health Promotion, Behaviour Change, and Community Needs Assessment

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cah recognition reasoning for Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) presenting with ambiguous genitalia, salt-wasting crisis in neonates, or precocious puberty/hirsutism in later-onset forms, and its glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid replacement management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Neglect.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of physical, medical, educational, or emotional neglect and distinguish neglect from failure to thrive of primarily organic etiology.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hypocalcemia workup reasoning for Hypocalcemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause of hypocalcemia (hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, CKD, and other causes) using PTH and vitamin D levels.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for End-of-Life Care.
candidates.source_competency_text: Develop a goals-of-care plan for a dying patient.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pediatric abdo pain ddx reasoning for Pediatric Abdominal Pain (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply a pediatric-specific differential diagnosis to abdominal pain, distinct from adult acute-abdomen etiologies.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply abdominal trauma mechanism reasoning for Abdominal and Genitourinary Trauma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate blunt vs. penetrating abdominal trauma mechanisms and associated organ injury patterns.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply vte prevention reasoning for Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pregnancy/postpartum as a VTE risk state, identify additional risk factors, and apply appropriate thromboprophylaxis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency recognition reasoning for Postpartum Mood Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize postpartum psychosis as a psychiatric emergency requiring urgent assessment given risk to both mother and infant.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sah recognition reasoning for Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize thunderclap headache as SAH until proven otherwise, and the urgent NCCT +/- LP (xanthochromia) diagnostic pathway.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pattern interpretation reasoning for Basic Pulmonary Function Test Interpretation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish obstructive, restrictive, mixed, and diffusion abnormalities on basic pulmonary function data.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Common Pediatric Renal Diseases.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use an anatomic (glomerular vs. tubulointerstitial vs. obstructive) framework to approach a child with an abnormal urinalysis or renal-function abnormality.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to Common Pediatric Renal Diseases

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sti reasoning for Sexually Transmitted Infections.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose and manage common sexually transmitted infections (chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HPV, HSV) in a primary-care patient, including partner notification and safer-sex counselling.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hypothermia reasoning for Intraoperative Temperature Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize and prevent intraoperative heat loss (forced-air warming, warmed fluids, humidified gases) as the dominant cause of perioperative hypothermia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Bleeding Disorders in Neonates.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize neonatal bleeding-disorder causes (vitamin K deficiency, sepsis-associated DIC, maternal-antibody-mediated neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia) and distinguish from normal birth-trauma-related bruising.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Cardiac Catheterization and Coronary Angiography.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications for cardiac catheterization (confirming CAD, guiding revascularization decisions).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply duration differential reasoning for Schizophreniform Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish schizophreniform disorder from schizophrenia and brief psychotic disorder principally by symptom duration (1-6 mo, vs. >6 mo for schizophrenia and <1 mo for brief psychotic disorder).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hierarchy of controls reasoning for Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the hierarchy of controls (elimination > substitution > engineering controls > administrative controls > PPE, most to least effective) to select the best primary-prevention intervention for an occupational hazard.
candidates.study_unit: Workplace Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Prevention

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis and management reasoning for Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize PDA's association with prematurity, the continuous machinery murmur with bounding pulses/wide pulse pressure, and that indomethacin (prostaglandin-E2 antagonist) is effective only in premature infants, with catheter/surgical closure reserved for term infants or persistent/complicated PDA.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation selection reasoning for Gynecologic Imaging and Endometrial Biopsy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select appropriate first-line imaging (pelvic ultrasound) and endometrial sampling for a patient with suspected structural or endometrial pathology, e.g. abnormal uterine bleeding.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply synthesis design selection reasoning for Summary Study Designs (Meta-Analysis, Systematic Review, Scoping Review).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish a meta-analysis (quantitative pooling), a systematic review (rigorous narrative synthesis), and a scoping review (mapping the literature without a single synthesized answer), and recognize publication bias and study heterogeneity as key meta-analysis limitations.
candidates.study_unit: Summary Study Designs (Meta-Analysis, Systematic Review, Scoping Review)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Tay-Sachs Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Tay-Sachs disease presenting in infancy with progressive neurodegeneration and a cherry-red macular spot, and identify population-based carrier-risk factors (e.g., Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry) relevant to preconception/prenatal counselling.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply male hypogonadism workup reasoning for Male Hypogonadism and Infertility.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish primary (testicular) from secondary (hypothalamic-pituitary) hypogonadism using LH/FSH and testosterone levels, and select testosterone replacement or fertility-preserving therapy accordingly.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Approach to Dizziness and Vertigo (DDx, Peripheral vs. Central Features, Evaluation).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish peripheral from central vertigo (acute continuous onset, abnormal head impulse test, multidirectional nystagmus, skew deviation, or the '5 Ds' of vertebrobasilar insufficiency all suggest a central/dangerous cause requiring urgent neuroimaging) and differentiate true vertigo from cardiac, psychogenic, and other non-vestibular dizziness.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to Dizziness and Vertigo (DDx, Peripheral vs. Central Features, Evaluation)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Blunt and Penetrating Ocular Trauma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of open-globe injury (peaked/irregular pupil, extruded uveal tissue, low IOP, positive Seidel sign) and know that further examination/manipulation is contraindicated -- apply a rigid shield and urgent ophthalmology/OR referral instead.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Laryngeal Carcinoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize persistent hoarseness (>2-3 wk) in a patient with smoking/alcohol use as a red flag for laryngeal carcinoma requiring laryngoscopy and biopsy, rather than symptomatic treatment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply anal fissure management reasoning for Anal Fissures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose anal fissure from history/exam and initiate first-line medical management before considering surgical sphincterotomy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply screening recommendations reasoning for Breast Cancer Screening Guidelines.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply current periodic-health-examination screening recommendations for breast cancer screening to a given patient's age/sex/risk profile, including when to start, stop, and how to interpret an abnormal result.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ces recognition reasoning for Cauda Equina Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize saddle anesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, and bilateral leg weakness as cauda equina syndrome requiring emergent MRI and surgical decompression.
