candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Schizophrenia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate an appropriate acute and maintenance management plan (antipsychotic pharmacotherapy, psychosocial supports, safety assessment).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize infants and children presenting with failure to thrive, developmental delay, or acute metabolic decompensation as possibly reflecting an inborn error of metabolism, and understand the role of universal newborn screening in early detection.
candidates.study_unit: Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply abuse recognition reasoning for Domestic Violence/Elder Abuse/Child Abuse.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs, symptoms, and risk situations for child abuse, elder abuse, and intimate partner/domestic violence, and initiate an appropriate safety-focused management plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognize reasoning for Fibromyalgia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize fibromyalgia after appropriate consideration of inflammatory and other mimics.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Malignant Hyperthermia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the clinical picture of malignant hyperthermia (rising ETCO2, tachycardia, muscle rigidity/trismus, late hyperthermia) as a life-threatening intraoperative emergency.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply interpretation reasoning for Assessment of Renal Function: GFR Measurement, Urinalysis, Urine Microscopy, and Urine Biochemistry.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret urinalysis (dipstick), urine microscopy (casts, crystals, cells), and urine biochemistry (electrolytes, FENa, osmolality) to distinguish glomerular from nonglomerular disease and prerenal from intrinsic renal causes of reduced function.
candidates.study_unit: Assessment of Renal Function: GFR Measurement, Urinalysis, Urine Microscopy, and Urine Biochemistry

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Malnutrition in Older Adults.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize malnutrition risk in an older adult (unintentional weight loss, reduced intake, social/functional barriers to eating) and initiate an appropriate nutritional assessment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Glomerular Disease: Nephritic/Nephrotic Syndrome Classification and Major Glomerulonephritides.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the major glomerulonephritis/nephrotic-syndrome entities (minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy, FSGS, MPGN, IgA-associated vasculitis) and their characteristic secondary associations.
candidates.study_unit: Glomerular Disease: Nephritic/Nephrotic Syndrome Classification and Major Glomerulonephritides

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pneumothorax recognition reasoning for Pneumothorax.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize simple, traumatic, and tension pneumothorax; distinguish tension pneumothorax as an immediate life threat requiring emergency needle decompression.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply abg interpretation reasoning for Arterial Blood Gases, Acid-Base Status, and Hypoxemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate, compensation, and oxygenation in common respiratory presentations.
candidates.study_unit: Arterial Blood Gases, Acid-Base Status, and Hypoxemia

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stenosis claudication reasoning for Lumbar Spinal Stenosis and Neurogenic Claudication.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate neurogenic claudication (relief with flexion/sitting) from vascular claudication in an older patient with back and leg pain.
candidates.study_unit: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis and Neurogenic Claudication

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess hemodynamic status first in pediatric UGIB and apply an age-specific differential (swallowed maternal blood in the neonate, esophagitis/gastritis, Mallory-Weiss tear, variceal bleeding in portal hypertension).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply choledocholithiasis recognition reasoning for Choledocholithiasis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize choledocholithiasis as a cause of obstructive jaundice and identify indications for ERCP.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cushing diagnosis reasoning for Cushing's Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Cushing's syndrome (central obesity, moon facies, striae, easy bruising, proximal myopathy) and apply the diagnostic algorithm (screening test, then localization to pituitary/adrenal/ectopic ACTH source).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply classification reasoning for Myopathies: Classification and Overview.
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify a myopathy by etiologic category (inflammatory, endocrine, toxic, infectious, hereditary dystrophy/metabolic/periodic-paralysis/mitochondrial) using the pattern of proximal vs. distal weakness and key investigations (CK, biopsy).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Sepsis and Septic Shock.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate timely sepsis bundle management (cultures, fluids, empiric antibiotics, source control).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stroke eligibility reasoning for Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Determine thrombolysis eligibility (time window, imaging findings, contraindications) for acute ischemic stroke.
candidates.study_unit: Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (ED Approach)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply anxiety reasoning for Anxiety.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose anxiety in a primary-care patient, assess severity/complications, and initiate an appropriate management plan (counselling, CBT referral, pharmacotherapy).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sexual assault approach reasoning for Sexual Assault (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Conduct a trauma-informed history and examination for a sexual assault patient, including forensic evidence considerations and referral pathways.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Pediatric Lymphadenopathy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish benign reactive lymphadenopathy from red-flag features (fixed/hard/matted nodes, >2 cm, supraclavicular location, systemic B symptoms, progressive growth) warranting biopsy for malignancy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Toddler's Diarrhea.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize toddler's diarrhea as a diagnosis of exclusion (chronic non-bloody diarrhea with undigested food particles in an otherwise well, normally-growing toddler, often related to excess fruit-juice intake), not requiring extensive workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Headache and Migraine.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate primary headache disorders (migraine, tension, cluster) from secondary causes using red-flag features, apply migraine diagnostic criteria, and outline abortive/prophylactic management while avoiding medication-overuse headache.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Shock: Recognition and Initial Stabilization.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize compensated and uncompensated shock and distinguish hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive, and obstructive patterns.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply interpretation reasoning for ECG Interpretation Fundamentals.
candidates.source_competency_text: Systematically interpret a 12-lead ECG (rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, ST/T changes) to identify ischemia, arrhythmia, and conduction abnormalities.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Achilles Tendon Pathology (Tendonitis and Rupture).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize acute Achilles tendon rupture (audible pop, palpable gap, positive Thompson test, unable to plantarflex against resistance) versus chronic Achilles tendinopathy, and know functional bracing is a reasonable non-operative option for rupture in low-demand patients.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply rct features reasoning for Experimental Study Designs (Randomized Controlled Trials).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify the key methodological features of an RCT (randomization, blinding level, control group) and explain why randomization is uniquely able to control for both measured and unmeasured confounding.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply acute diarrhea diagnosis reasoning for Acute Diarrhea (including Traveller's Diarrhea).
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of acute diarrhea (lasting <1 week), with particular attention to risk factors for specific causes (including travel) and assessment for dehydration/electrolyte complications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize COPD, confirm persistent airflow obstruction, and assess symptoms and exacerbation risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Humeral Shaft Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize humeral shaft fracture as the classic cause of radial nerve injury (wrist drop, sensory loss over dorsal first web space) and document neurovascular status before and after any reduction/splinting.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the FASD diagnostic triad (characteristic facial features, growth restriction, CNS/neurodevelopmental abnormalities) and its basis in prenatal alcohol exposure.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hazard category recognition reasoning for Occupational Hazards by Category (Physical, Chemical, Biological, Psychosocial, Ergonomic, Safety).
candidates.source_competency_text: Given an occupational exposure and clinical presentation (e.g., noise -> hearing loss, benzene -> AML, asbestos -> mesothelioma, silica -> silicosis), classify the hazard category and identify the associated health effect.
candidates.study_unit: Occupational Hazards by Category (Physical, Chemical, Biological, Psychosocial, Ergonomic, Safety)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Panic Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose panic disorder (recurrent unexpected panic attacks plus >=1 mo of persistent concern/worry about additional attacks or maladaptive behavioural change) and distinguish from a medical mimicker (e.g., cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary) causing panic-like symptoms.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis management reasoning for Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize brief, positionally-triggered vertigo as BPPV, confirm with the Dix-Hallpike maneuver, and know first-line treatment is a canalith repositioning maneuver (e.g. Epley) rather than pharmacotherapy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply counselling reasoning for Menopause.
candidates.source_competency_text: Explain the physiology and expected symptoms of menopause and counsel on prevention/management of its undesirable effects (vasomotor symptoms, bone/cardiovascular risk, genitourinary syndrome).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply masld recognition reasoning for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize MASLD as the most common cause of chronic liver disease in patients with metabolic syndrome and its progression risk to steatohepatitis/cirrhosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Hypertension: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis, Renovascular Hypertension, and Renal Parenchymal Hypertension.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate chronic (benign) from malignant hypertensive nephrosclerosis using clinical picture, urinalysis, and target-organ-damage findings; recognize renovascular hypertension as a secondary, potentially reversible cause.
candidates.study_unit: Hypertension: Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis, Renovascular Hypertension, and Renal Parenchymal Hypertension

candidates.principal_decision: Apply complication recognition reasoning for Multiple Myeloma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hypercalcemia, renal failure, and pathologic fracture/cord compression as urgent myeloma complications requiring prompt management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize PPHN (severe hypoxemia out of proportion to CXR findings, differential pre-/post-ductal saturations, echo showing elevated pulmonary pressures without structural CHD) as a cause of refractory neonatal cyanosis.
candidates.study_unit: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn

candidates.principal_decision: Apply variceal bleed management reasoning for Esophageal Varices.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize esophageal varices secondary to portal hypertension as a high-risk cause of upper GI bleeding and initiate emergency resuscitation and hemorrhage-control measures.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ecological fallacy reasoning for Observational Study Designs (Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional, Ecological).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize an ecological fallacy when population-level associations are incorrectly extrapolated to individuals.
candidates.study_unit: Observational Study Designs (Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional, Ecological)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Meniere's Disease (Endolymphatic Hydrops).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the classic tetrad (episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency SNHL, tinnitus, aural fullness) and know first-line management is a low-salt diet and diuretics before escalation to intratympanic or surgical therapy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply vent complications reasoning for Oxygen Therapy and Mechanical Ventilation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize airway, alveolar, cardiovascular, and metabolic complications of positive-pressure mechanical ventilation, and interpret abnormal ETCO2 trends against their common causes (Table 3).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Hallucinogen Use.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the characteristic intoxication/withdrawal presentation and health consequences of this substance.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis and management reasoning for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply DSM-5 inattentive/hyperactive-impulsive criteria (symptoms in 2+ settings, onset before age 12) to diagnose ADHD, recognize common comorbidities (learning disorder, anxiety, ODD), and outline first-line management (behavioural strategies +/- stimulant medication).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Gestational Trophoblastic Disease/Neoplasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize molar pregnancy (hydatidiform mole) from its classic presentation (markedly elevated beta-hCG, uterus large-for-dates, first-trimester bleeding, hyperemesis) and its malignant sequela (choriocarcinoma).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply burn severity triage reasoning for Burns (incl. Inhalation Injury).
candidates.source_competency_text: Estimate burn severity/TBSA and apply admission criteria, including escharotomy indications for circumferential burns.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Lid Swelling and Inflammatory/Infectious Lid Lesions (Hordeolum, Chalazion, Blepharitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate hordeolum (acute, painful, infectious) from chalazion (chronic, painless, granulomatous) and recognize blepharitis as a chronic lid-margin condition managed with lid hygiene.
candidates.study_unit: Lid Swelling and Inflammatory/Infectious Lid Lesions (Hordeolum, Chalazion, Blepharitis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply communication reasoning for Pedigree Analysis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Affirm a gender-diverse patient's gender identity while separately clarifying sex assigned at birth/chromosomal sex where genetically relevant to pedigree construction.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply history taking reasoning for Well-Child Visit Overview (Approach to the Pediatric History and Periodic Health Encounter).
candidates.source_competency_text: Structure a pediatric history around age-specific concerns: family history (consanguinity, recurrent losses, early deaths), social history (caregivers, school/daycare adjustment, safety, stability), and the HEEADSSS/SSHADESS framework and ITHELPS social-determinants screen for adolescents.
candidates.study_unit: Well-Child Visit Overview (Approach to the Pediatric History and Periodic Health Encounter)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Chronic Kidney Disease: KDIGO Staging, Complications, and Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Construct a comprehensive management plan for CKD progression prevention (BP/glycemic control, RAAS blockade, SGLT2i) and complications (anemia, mineral bone disease, metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia).
candidates.study_unit: Chronic Kidney Disease: KDIGO Staging, Complications, and Management

candidates.principal_decision: Apply arrest algorithm reasoning for Appendices: Advanced Cardiac Life Support Guidelines.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the adult cardiac arrest algorithm (CPR quality metrics, shockable vs. non-shockable pathway, epinephrine/amiodarone dosing, advanced airway timing).
candidates.study_unit: Appendices: Advanced Cardiac Life Support Guidelines

candidates.principal_decision: Apply complications reasoning for Congestive Heart Failure.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize complications of chronic heart failure (arrhythmia, renal dysfunction, cardiorenal syndrome).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply portal htn recognition reasoning for Portal Hypertension.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize portal hypertension as the mechanism underlying variceal bleeding and ascites in cirrhosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply serum sickness reasoning for Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize serum sickness-like reaction (symmetrical urticarial eruption, malaise, arthralgia 1-3 wk after drug exposure) and distinguish it from true serum sickness.
candidates.study_unit: Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction

candidates.principal_decision: Apply localization reasoning for Stroke: Terminology, Pathophysiology, and Vascular Territory Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a described stroke deficit pattern, localize to a vascular territory (ACA, MCA, PCA) and distinguish ischemic mechanism (large-vessel, small-vessel/lacunar, cardioembolic, systemic hypoperfusion) from hemorrhagic stroke.
candidates.study_unit: Stroke: Terminology, Pathophysiology, and Vascular Territory Syndromes

candidates.principal_decision: Apply gdm management reasoning for Diabetes Mellitus in Pregnancy (Gestational Diabetes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize risk factors and screening approach for gestational diabetes, and outline glycemic-management and delivery-timing implications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply symptom control reasoning for Pain and Symptom Management (WHO Pain Ladder, Table of Common Symptoms).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select an appropriate first-line pharmacologic or non-pharmacologic approach for a common palliative symptom (pain, dyspnea, nausea/vomiting, constipation, delirium/agitation, secretions) using the WHO pain-ladder stepwise-escalation principle and general symptom-management categories.
candidates.study_unit: Pain and Symptom Management (WHO Pain Ladder, Table of Common Symptoms)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cultural safety reasoning for Concepts of Health, Health Equity, and Cultural Safety.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish cultural humility, cultural safety, cultural awareness, cultural sensitivity, and cultural competency as a spectrum of approaches to culturally appropriate care.
candidates.study_unit: Concepts of Health, Health Equity, and Cultural Safety

candidates.principal_decision: Apply anticipatory guidance reasoning for Dentition and Caries.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize normal primary-tooth eruption timing and early childhood caries risk factors (prolonged bottle/breastfeeding at night, sugary liquids) as an anticipatory-guidance topic.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Pediatric Bone Tumours.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize red flags for osteosarcoma (adolescent, distal femur/proximal tibia, night pain, sunburst periosteal reaction) and Ewing sarcoma (diaphyseal, onion-skin periosteal reaction, may mimic infection with fever/elevated inflammatory markers) as malignant causes of bone pain requiring urgent imaging.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply spinal trauma assessment reasoning for Spinal Cord Injury and Fractures of the Spine.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of spinal cord injury after trauma, apply spinal immobilization principles, and identify unstable spine fracture patterns requiring urgent imaging/referral.
candidates.study_unit: Spinal Cord Injury and Fractures of the Spine

candidates.principal_decision: Apply risk assessment reasoning for Falls.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify intrinsic (sensory, cognitive, musculoskeletal, medication) and extrinsic (environmental) fall risk factors in an older adult.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment and management reasoning for Approach to the Infant/Child with Dehydration.
candidates.source_competency_text: Clinically classify dehydration severity (mild/moderate/severe) using history and exam findings (capillary refill, mucous membranes, skin turgor, urine output, mental status) and select oral rehydration therapy vs. IV fluid resuscitation accordingly.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to the Infant/Child with Dehydration

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Hypoxemic and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish hypoxemic from hypercapnic respiratory failure using clinical findings and ABGs and identify acute-on-chronic physiology.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply kinetics order reasoning for Pharmacokinetic Parameters and Dosing Strategy (Half-Life, Clearance, Steady-State, Loading/Maintenance Dosing).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish first-order from zero-order (non-linear/saturation) elimination kinetics and recognize the clinical drugs where zero-order kinetics becomes relevant at therapeutic or toxic doses (phenytoin, alcohol, high-dose ASA).
candidates.study_unit: Pharmacokinetic Parameters and Dosing Strategy (Half-Life, Clearance, Steady-State, Loading/Maintenance Dosing)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply counselling reasoning for Prostate Cancer Recognition and PSA Context.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize concerning prostate presentations and discuss PSA uncertainty without applying a fixed screening schedule.
candidates.study_unit: Prostate Cancer Recognition and PSA Context

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sleep disorders reasoning for Sleep Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose common primary-care sleep disorders (e.g., insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea) and initiate an appropriate management plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Peripheral/Local Edema.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish unilateral/localized edema from systemic cardiac edema.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment and prevention reasoning for Drowning/Submersion Injuries.
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess severity and pulmonary/neurologic complications of a submersion injury and initiate stabilization, and counsel on drowning-prevention strategies (supervision, pool fencing, swim lessons) given children are the population at highest risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply skin systemic association reasoning for Skin Manifestations of Systemic Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize named cutaneous signs of systemic disease (e.g., dermatomyositis heliotrope rash/Gottron's papules, acanthosis nigricans as an insulin-resistance marker, Paget's disease of the nipple, necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum) and connect them to the underlying diagnosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply public health reasoning for Tuberculosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize TB as a reportable disease requiring Public Health notification and contact investigation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply mse components reasoning for Mental Status Examination.
candidates.source_competency_text: Perform and document a structured mental status examination (appearance/behaviour, attitude, speech, mood/affect, perception, thought process, thought content, insight, judgment, cognition), distinguishing key descriptive terms (e.g., circumstantial vs. tangential vs. flight of ideas; hallucination vs. illusion; delusion vs. overvalued idea).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Analgesic Nephropathies: NSAID- and Acetaminophen-Induced Renal Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize NSAID- and acetaminophen-associated renal syndromes (vasomotor AKI, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, papillary necrosis) and their reversibility with drug discontinuation.
candidates.study_unit: Analgesic Nephropathies: NSAID- and Acetaminophen-Induced Renal Syndromes

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Cardiac Arrest / Sudden Cardiac Death.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize shockable vs. non-shockable rhythms.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify the initial investigations for a child with suspected acute metabolic decompensation (electrolytes/anion gap, blood glucose, lactate/ammonia, urine studies) and the principle of discontinuing feeds pending workup.
candidates.study_unit: Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply complications reasoning for Myocarditis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize risk of arrhythmia and fulminant heart failure in myocarditis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply vascular lesion ddx reasoning for Vascular Lesions and Malformations (Hemangioma, Vascular Malformations, Spider/Cherry Angioma, Pyogenic Granuloma).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish common benign vascular lesions (spider angioma, cherry angioma, pyogenic granuloma, port-wine stain) by clinical features.
candidates.study_unit: Vascular Lesions and Malformations (Hemangioma, Vascular Malformations, Spider/Cherry Angioma, Pyogenic Granuloma)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply medication management reasoning for Preoperative Medications and Fasting Guidelines.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify which chronic medications (anticoagulants, ACEI/ARB, oral hypoglycemics, steroids) require holding, adjusting, or continuing through the perioperative period.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply class recognition reasoning for Mood Stabilizers.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the indications, class-characteristic adverse effects, and rational-use principles of mood stabilizers as a drug class, without hard-coding specific current dosing, sequencing, or monitoring-schedule recommendations (verified independently against current guidance at question-generation stage).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply adr classification reasoning for Adverse Drug Reactions: Classification and Clinical Approach.
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify a suspected adverse drug reaction using the Type A-E framework (Augmented/dose-related, Bizarre/idiosyncratic, Chronic/cumulative, Delayed, End-of-use/withdrawal) to predict its likely mechanism and management approach.
candidates.study_unit: Adverse Drug Reactions: Classification and Clinical Approach

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initiation reasoning for Opioid Therapy for Chronic Non-Cancer Pain.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the principle of optimizing non-opioid pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic therapy before initiating opioid therapy for chronic non-cancer pain.
candidates.study_unit: Opioid Therapy for Chronic Non-Cancer Pain

candidates.principal_decision: Apply labour analgesia reasoning for Obstetrical Anesthesia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Compare systemic, inhalational, and neuraxial labour analgesia options by onset, completeness of analgesia, and maternal/fetal risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Exercise/Pharmacologic Stress Testing.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize appropriate candidates for stress testing (intermediate-probability stable chest pain) and contraindications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pct recognition reasoning for Dermatitis Herpetiformis and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize porphyria cutanea tarda by photo-exposed skin fragility/bullae and its associations with hepatitis C, alcohol use, and estrogen therapy.
candidates.study_unit: Dermatitis Herpetiformis and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Pediatric Bleeding Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use history/exam pattern (mucocutaneous/petechial bleeding suggests platelet or vWD; deep muscle/joint bleeding suggests factor deficiency) and screening coagulation tests (PT, PTT, platelet count) to localize a pediatric bleeding disorder.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hemangioma recognition reasoning for Vascular Lesions and Malformations (Hemangioma, Vascular Malformations, Spider/Cherry Angioma, Pyogenic Granuloma).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize infantile hemangioma and its natural history, and identify features warranting early specialist referral (functional impairment, ulceration, high-risk location).
candidates.study_unit: Vascular Lesions and Malformations (Hemangioma, Vascular Malformations, Spider/Cherry Angioma, Pyogenic Granuloma)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pv diagnosis reasoning for Pemphigus Vulgaris and Pemphigus Foliaceus.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pemphigus vulgaris by flaccid, non-pruritic, predominantly mucosal-onset bullae, positive Nikolsky sign, and anti-desmoglein-1/3 IgG on immunofluorescence.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply jaundice ddx surgical reasoning for Differential Diagnosis of Jaundice (Surgical Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate surgical (obstructive) from non-surgical causes of jaundice and identify indications for biliary decompression or surgical referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition and urgency reasoning for Pediatric Vasculitides (HSP, Kawasaki Disease).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Kawasaki disease's principal clinical criteria (fever >=5 d plus conjunctivitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, mucositis, extremity changes) and the urgency of IVIG treatment within 10 d of fever onset to prevent coronary artery aneurysm; recognize Henoch-Schonlein purpura's tetrad (palpable purpura, arthritis, abdominal pain, renal involvement) with a normal platelet count distinguishing it from ITP.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Acid-Base Disorders: Metabolic Acidosis and Metabolic Alkalosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis using anion gap, osmolar gap, and expected compensation.
candidates.study_unit: Acid-Base Disorders: Metabolic Acidosis and Metabolic Alkalosis

candidates.principal_decision: Apply lumbar disc recognition reasoning for Lumbar Disc Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sciatica from lumbar disc herniation and the indications for imaging vs. conservative management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency recognition reasoning for Oncologic Emergencies: Hyperviscosity Syndrome and Tumour Lysis Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hyperviscosity syndrome (mucosal bleeding, visual changes, neurologic symptoms in a patient with a high M-protein or extreme leukocytosis) and initiate urgent plasmapheresis/leukapheresis.
candidates.study_unit: Oncologic Emergencies: Hyperviscosity Syndrome and Tumour Lysis Syndrome

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Autism Spectrum Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize core features of autism spectrum disorder (persistent deficits in social communication/interaction, restricted/repetitive behaviours and interests) and the role of early screening and referral for intensive behavioural intervention.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ras recognition reasoning for Oral Diseases (Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize recurrent aphthous stomatitis (canker sores) by painful, shallow, round-to-oval mucosal ulcers with a creamy-white pseudomembrane, and distinguish from Behcet syndrome/HSV in the differential.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply screening reasoning for Retinopathy of Prematurity.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize preterm/low-birth-weight infants (especially with supplemental oxygen exposure) as requiring ROP screening given its potential for retinal detachment and vision loss if untreated.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply joint pain approach reasoning for Joint Pain.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply a structured approach to a patient with joint pain (acuity/severity triage, articular vs. nonarticular, mono- vs. polyarticular) to guide further workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Asthma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize asthma and confirm variable airflow limitation using appropriate objective testing.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply manage reasoning for Polymyalgia rheumatica.
candidates.source_competency_text: Arrange appropriate assessment and urgent escalation if visual-risk symptoms occur.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Chest Pain (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify red-flag features requiring immediate stabilization and urgent referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply optimization reasoning for Preoperative Cardiopulmonary and Airway-Risk Optimization.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply comorbidity-specific perioperative management (continue antihypertensives, respect ACC/AHA post-MI surgical delay, use protected airway/RSI in aspiration risk).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply interview structure reasoning for Psychiatric History Taking.
candidates.source_competency_text: Conduct a structured psychiatric history (identifying data, chief complaint, HPI, psychiatric functional inquiry including safety screening, past psychiatric/medical/substance/developmental history, collateral history) as the foundation for every psychiatric diagnostic objective in this chapter.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dm diagnosis reasoning for Diabetes Mellitus: Classification and Diagnosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply Diabetes Canada 2018 diagnostic criteria (FPG >=7.0, A1c >=6.5%, 2h OGTT >=11.1, or random PG >=11.1 with symptoms) to diagnose diabetes mellitus.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns (Triplet Repeat Expansion/Anticipation, Imprinting/Uniparental Disomy, Mitochondrial Inheritance).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize triplet-repeat anticipation, genomic imprinting/uniparental disomy, and mitochondrial (maternal) inheritance as distinct non-Mendelian inheritance mechanisms, with awareness of their prototypical example conditions (e.g., Fragile X, Huntington disease, Prader-Willi/Angelman syndromes).
candidates.study_unit: Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns (Triplet Repeat Expansion/Anticipation, Imprinting/Uniparental Disomy, Mitochondrial Inheritance)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply rct limitations reasoning for Experimental Study Designs (Randomized Controlled Trials).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize situations where an RCT is not feasible or ethical (e.g., harmful exposures) and identify threats to RCT validity (contamination, co-intervention, loss to follow-up, poor generalizability).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply glycemic targets reasoning for Treatment of Diabetes: Glycemic Targets, Lifestyle, and Pharmacotherapy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Individualize A1c targets by patient frailty, functional dependence, and hypoglycemia risk.
candidates.study_unit: Treatment of Diabetes: Glycemic Targets, Lifestyle, and Pharmacotherapy

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Valve Intervention: Repair/Replacement and Prosthetic Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications for valve intervention (severe symptomatic disease, declining ventricular function).
candidates.study_unit: Valve Intervention: Repair/Replacement and Prosthetic Management

candidates.principal_decision: Apply urgency reasoning for Pulmonary Hypertension.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize decompensated right-heart failure or high-risk symptoms requiring urgent referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Smith's Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish Smith's fracture (volar displacement, 'garden spade' deformity, typically from a fall onto a flexed wrist) from Colles' fracture (dorsal displacement).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome / Pre-Excitation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the need to avoid AV-nodal blocking agents in WPW-associated tachyarrhythmia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply legal professional action reasoning for End-of-Life Care.
candidates.source_competency_text: Know the provisions of Canadian MAID law and respond appropriately to a MAID request.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply exacerbation reasoning for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify and initially manage an acute COPD exacerbation, including respiratory-failure risk and escalation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Retinal Artery Occlusion (Central/Branch).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize CRAO (sudden painless profound vision loss, cherry-red spot, afferent pupillary defect) as an ocular stroke equivalent requiring immediate ophthalmology/stroke-protocol activation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply next step reasoning for Basic Chest Radiograph Patterns.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use the radiographic pattern with clinical context to select appropriate further assessment or referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply mastitis management reasoning for Mastitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize mastitis, distinguish it from breast abscess, and initiate management while supporting continued breastfeeding.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Nuclear Medicine Thyroid Imaging (Radioactive Iodine Uptake, Scintiscan Hot/Cold Nodules, Radioiodine Ablation).
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret RAIU as elevated in hyperthyroid states with increased thyroid synthesis (Graves', toxic multinodular goitre) versus decreased in thyroiditis or exogenous hormone use, and recognize that a 'cold' nodule on thyroid scintiscan requires biopsy to exclude malignancy while a 'hot' nodule is reassuring.
candidates.study_unit: Nuclear Medicine Thyroid Imaging (Radioactive Iodine Uptake, Scintiscan Hot/Cold Nodules, Radioiodine Ablation)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention reasoning for Sickle Cell Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize preventive measures (vaccination, prophylactic penicillin in children, hydroxyurea) and screening for chronic complications (stroke risk, retinopathy, pulmonary hypertension).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply alcohol screening reasoning for Alcohol Use.
candidates.source_competency_text: Screen for unhealthy alcohol use and initiate brief intervention or referral as appropriate in the primary-care setting.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Pediatric Craniofacial Anomalies.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize common pediatric craniofacial anomalies (cleft lip/palate, craniosynostosis) on newborn/infant exam and identify the need for early multidisciplinary craniofacial-team referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply error prone terms reasoning for Dangerous Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the ISMP Canada list of dangerous abbreviations, symbols, and dose designations (U, IU, QD/QOD, trailing zeros, lack of leading zero, ambiguous drug abbreviations) and apply the recommended safe alternative when writing or reviewing a prescription/order.
candidates.study_unit: Dangerous Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations

candidates.principal_decision: Apply climate health hazards reasoning for Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Public Health Response.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify the mechanism by which a given climate-related hazard (extreme weather, air quality, vector range shift, food/water insecurity) produces a specific health effect.
candidates.study_unit: Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Public Health Response

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Wilson Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Wilson disease presenting with liver disease, movement disorder, and/or Kayser-Fleischer rings in a young patient, and initiate chelation therapy referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sampling methods reasoning for Population, Sampling Methods, and Sample Size.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish probability sampling methods (simple/systematic/stratified random, cluster) from non-probability methods (convenience, snowball) and identify an appropriate method for a given research scenario.
candidates.study_unit: Population, Sampling Methods, and Sample Size

candidates.principal_decision: Apply fluid choice reasoning for Perioperative Fluid Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select balanced crystalloid over normal saline for routine resuscitation, and apply appropriate replacement ratios (3:1 crystalloid, 1:1 colloid) for intraoperative blood loss.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Branchial Cleft Cysts, Sinuses, and Fistulae.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize a lateral neck cyst/sinus/fistula (classically anterior to the sternocleidomastoid) as a branchial cleft anomaly and know it should be surgically excised rather than incised and drained if infected.
candidates.study_unit: Branchial Cleft Cysts, Sinuses, and Fistulae

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate an appropriate initial management plan addressing menstrual regulation, fertility goals, and metabolic risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply indications and complications reasoning for Hysterectomy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the major indications (e.g., refractory AUB, symptomatic fibroids, malignancy, prolapse) and major complications for hysterectomy at a level sufficient to counsel and refer a patient appropriately.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Polycythemia Vera.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize thrombosis as the major PV complication and therapeutic phlebotomy plus low-dose aspirin as first-line management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Iron Metabolism and Iron Deficiency Anemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret iron studies (ferritin, TIBC, transferrin saturation) to diagnose iron deficiency and distinguish it from other microcytic anemias.
candidates.study_unit: Iron Metabolism and Iron Deficiency Anemia

candidates.principal_decision: Apply cholelithiasis management reasoning for Cholelithiasis and Biliary Colic.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize symptomatic cholelithiasis (biliary colic) and identify indications for elective cholecystectomy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency recognition reasoning for Thrombotic Microangiopathies (TTP/HUS).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the pentad/features of TTP (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, +/- neurologic changes, renal dysfunction, fever) and HUS (typically post-diarrheal, renal-predominant) as medical emergencies.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Salivary Gland Neoplasms (incl. Parotid Gland Neoplasms).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that the smaller the salivary gland, the higher the likelihood a mass within it is malignant (parotid masses are usually benign; minor salivary gland masses are usually malignant), and that facial nerve (CN VII) palsy with a parotid mass is a red flag for malignant invasion requiring urgent workup (FNA, imaging).
candidates.study_unit: Salivary Gland Neoplasms (incl. Parotid Gland Neoplasms)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition and urgency reasoning for Infantile Spasms (West Syndrome).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize infantile spasms (brief symmetric flexion/extension contractions in clusters, onset 4-8 mo, hypsarrhythmia on EEG) as a pediatric emergency requiring urgent identification and treatment to minimize developmental-regression risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Sex Chromosome Disorders and Fragile X Syndrome (Turner Syndrome, Klinefelter Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the characteristic phenotype and key complications of Turner syndrome (short stature, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea), Klinefelter syndrome (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, infertility), and Fragile X syndrome (intellectual disability, macroorchidism, premutation-related risks).
candidates.study_unit: Sex Chromosome Disorders and Fragile X Syndrome (Turner Syndrome, Klinefelter Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Airway Problems in Children and Signs of Airway Obstruction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of impending airway obstruction in a child (stridor, drooling, tripod positioning, retractions, cyanosis) and apply the general principle of minimizing agitation/avoiding unnecessary exam maneuvers (e.g. tongue depressor) that could precipitate complete obstruction in a child with a tenuous airway.
candidates.study_unit: Airway Problems in Children and Signs of Airway Obstruction

candidates.principal_decision: Apply uterine rupture recognition reasoning for Uterine Rupture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of uterine rupture (fetal bradycardia, loss of station, abdominal pain, especially in a trial of labour after Caesarean) and initiate emergent management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply addisons recognition reasoning for Adrenocortical Insufficiency (Addison's Disease, Adrenal Crisis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease: fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) and distinguish from secondary adrenal insufficiency (no hyperpigmentation, normal aldosterone axis).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Conduct Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose conduct disorder (pattern violating others' rights/age-appropriate norms across aggression, property destruction, deceitfulness/theft, or rule violation) and recognize childhood-onset (before age 10) carries worse prognosis and higher risk of progression to antisocial personality disorder.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply renal colic workup reasoning for Nephrolithiasis (Renal Colic).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize renal colic presentation and select appropriate imaging (CT KUB) and analgesia-first management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply thyroid storm reasoning for Thyrotoxic Crisis / Thyroid Storm.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize thyroid storm (fever, tachyarrhythmia, altered mental status in a thyrotoxic patient) and initiate emergency management (beta-blockade, thionamides, iodine, steroids).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Bipolar Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose bipolar I disorder (>=1 manic episode), bipolar II disorder (hypomanic + major depressive episodes), and cyclothymia, distinguishing mania from hypomania by severity/duration/functional impairment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply metsyn criteria reasoning for Metabolic Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply diagnostic criteria for metabolic syndrome (waist circumference, triglycerides, HDL, blood pressure, fasting glucose) and counsel on lifestyle-based risk reduction.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ecg recognition reasoning for Chest Pain (ED Approach, incl. Life-Threatening ECG Changes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize life-threatening ECG changes (STEMI-equivalents, malignant dysrhythmias).
candidates.study_unit: Chest Pain (ED Approach, incl. Life-Threatening ECG Changes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply antenatal depression screening reasoning for Antenatal Depression.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize risk factors and screening indications for antenatal depression during routine prenatal visits.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Frailty.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize frailty as a distinct clinical syndrome (e.g., unintentional weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, slow gait, low activity) rather than normal aging.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply legal professional action reasoning for Physician-Industry Relations.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize and appropriately manage conflicts of interest arising from industry relationships.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate management (trauma-focused psychotherapy first-line; SSRIs/SNRIs as pharmacologic option; prazosin can help trauma-related nightmares).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply class recognition reasoning for Antipsychotics.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the indications, class-characteristic adverse effects, and rational-use principles of antipsychotics as a drug class, without hard-coding specific current dosing, sequencing, or monitoring-schedule recommendations (verified independently against current guidance at question-generation stage).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hypoglycemia treatment reasoning for Hypoglycemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Treat hypoglycemia urgently with oral carbohydrate, D50W IV, or glucagon IM/SC, prioritizing treatment over diagnosis in the acute setting.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Gastroenteritis (Pediatric, GI Chapter).
candidates.source_competency_text: Manage acute pediatric gastroenteritis with oral rehydration therapy as first-line treatment, recognize indications for IV fluids, and counsel on the self-limited course of most viral gastroenteritis (rotavirus, norovirus).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Epicondylitis (Tennis/Golfer's Elbow).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize lateral ('tennis elbow') and medial ('golfer's elbow') epicondylitis clinically and know first-line management is non-operative (rest, bracing, physiotherapy).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Familial Cancer Syndromes (Li-Fraumeni, Lynch, FAP, Hereditary Breast/Ovarian Cancer, Von Hippel-Lindau, Cowden, Neurofibromatosis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the gene and associated cancer pattern for the most clinically significant hereditary cancer syndromes (e.g., BRCA1/2-Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer, MSH2/MLH1-Lynch syndrome, APC-FAP, TP53-Li-Fraumeni) as a trigger for genetics referral and enhanced surveillance.
candidates.study_unit: Familial Cancer Syndromes (Li-Fraumeni, Lynch, FAP, Hereditary Breast/Ovarian Cancer, Von Hippel-Lindau, Cowden, Neurofibromatosis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Pediatric Respiratory Distress/Dyspnea.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the ABC-first, sick-vs-not-sick framework and an upper-airway (foreign body, croup) vs. lower-airway (bronchiolitis, pneumonia, asthma) localization approach to a child presenting with respiratory distress.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply secondary dyslipidemia reasoning for Secondary Dyslipidemias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify and treat underlying causes of secondary dyslipidemia (diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, medications) before or alongside lipid-lowering therapy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply drug urticaria recognition reasoning for Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize drug-induced urticaria/angioedema and assess for concurrent anaphylaxis (bronchospasm, laryngeal edema, shock) requiring emergency management.
candidates.study_unit: Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Polyuria: Diagnostic Approach.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause of polyuria using a stepwise urine-osmolality-based approach (water diuresis vs. osmotic diuresis vs. mixed).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply device choice reasoning for Methods of Supporting the Airway.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select the least invasive airway device adequate for a given clinical scenario (spontaneously ventilating low-risk patient vs. aspiration risk vs. positive-pressure ventilation need) and recognize each device's key contraindication.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dka recognition reasoning for Acute Complications of Diabetes (DKA, HHS).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize DKA precipitants ('8 I's') and initiate emergency management (fluids, insulin, potassium repletion).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply mortality measures reasoning for Measures of Mortality and Disease Burden.
candidates.source_competency_text: Calculate and interpret crude death rate, infant mortality rate, and maternal mortality rate.
candidates.study_unit: Measures of Mortality and Disease Burden

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pediatric communication reasoning for Pediatric Symptom Management (Unique Considerations).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that open, developmentally-matched communication with the child about diagnosis/prognosis reduces anxiety, and that shared decision-making with both child (to the extent possible) and parents guides pediatric EOL care.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Urological Imaging (KUB, Renal Colic and Renal Mass CT incl. Bosniak Classification, Retrograde Studies, Renal Nuclear Scan).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select the appropriate initial imaging modality for suspected renal colic (CT KUB) and for hematuria/suspected renal mass (CT urography, triphasic CT), and apply the Bosniak classification to determine whether a cystic renal mass requires follow-up or urological referral.
candidates.study_unit: Urological Imaging (KUB, Renal Colic and Renal Mass CT incl. Bosniak Classification, Retrograde Studies, Renal Nuclear Scan)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dementia reasoning for Dementia (Major Neurocognitive Disorder).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify cognitive decline in a primary-care patient, look for reversible risk factors, and differentiate early Alzheimer disease from other causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply indications reasoning for Breast Reduction (Reduction Mammaplasty).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the symptomatic indications for breast reduction (musculoskeletal pain, bra-strap grooving, intertrigo) as distinct from a diagnostic breast-mass workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Bradyarrhythmias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify hemodynamically unstable bradycardia requiring urgent intervention.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigations reasoning for Preoperative Assessment (History, Investigations, ASA Classification).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select preoperative investigations appropriate to comorbidity/procedure risk rather than ordering a fixed panel for every patient.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Palpitations.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize palpitations warranting urgent vs. non-urgent evaluation based on hemodynamic stability.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hypertrichosis recognition reasoning for Alopecia (Non-Scarring and Scarring) and Hypertrichosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hypertrichosis as excessive hair growth independent of androgen effect, distinct from hirsutism.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognize reasoning for Reactive arthritis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize a postinfectious asymmetric arthritis with ocular or genitourinary features.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply tolac counselling reasoning for Trial of Labour After Caesarean (TOLAC).
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess candidacy for trial of labour after Caesarean and counsel on the relative risks/benefits versus repeat Caesarean, including uterine rupture risk.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Acute Epiglottitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize rapid-onset high fever, drooling, muffled voice, and tripod/sniffing positioning as epiglottitis, avoid agitating the child or examining the oropharynx/using a tongue depressor (risk of precipitating complete obstruction), and secure the airway in a controlled setting (OR) before further workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis (incl. Orbital/Intracranial Complications).
candidates.source_competency_text: Use symptom-duration criteria (persistent >10 d, worsening after 5 d, or severe symptoms with high fever/purulence for 3-4 d) to distinguish acute bacterial from viral rhinosinusitis, and recognize periorbital swelling, proptosis, or ophthalmoplegia as orbital extension requiring urgent imaging and IV antibiotics.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Growing Pains.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose growing pains as a diagnosis of exclusion (bilateral lower-extremity pain, typically evening/nighttime, normal exam, no morning stiffness/limp/swelling) and recognize red flags that argue against it (unilateral pain, joint swelling, systemic symptoms, morning stiffness).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Tracheoesophageal Fistula.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize TEF/esophageal atresia by inability to pass an NG tube, choking/cyanosis/coughing with first feeds, and polyhydramnios antenatally; recognize the VACTERL association.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hemochromatosis recognition reasoning for Hemochromatosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize hereditary hemochromatosis (elevated ferritin/transferrin saturation, classic triad) as a cause of liver disease and initiate iron-studies-based diagnosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply postop urinary renal reasoning for Postoperative Urinary and Renal Complications.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize and initiate management of postoperative urinary retention and acute kidney injury.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply examination reasoning for Approach to the Patient with Physical Differences (Dysmorphology Assessment).
candidates.source_competency_text: Perform a systematic dysmorphology physical examination (craniofacial, ocular, otic, spinal, limb features) and compare findings against family members.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to the Patient with Physical Differences (Dysmorphology Assessment)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Apnea of Prematurity.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish normal periodic breathing from pathologic apnea (>20 s, or shorter with bradycardia/desaturation), classify as central/obstructive/mixed, and recognize apnea of prematurity vs. apnea as a sign of underlying illness (sepsis, NEC) requiring sepsis workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dystocia recognition reasoning for Abnormal Progression of Labour (Dystocia).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize abnormal progression of labour (protraction/arrest disorders) using partogram-based criteria and outline the management options.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply postpartum fever workup reasoning for Postpartum Fever.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply a structured differential (the '7 Ws'-type framework) to postpartum fever and identify indications for urgent investigation/treatment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Sexual Dysfunction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize DSM-5 sexual dysfunction categories (desire, arousal, orgasmic, and pain disorders) and screen for contributing medical, psychiatric, and medication (e.g., SSRI) causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply lbo management reasoning for Large Bowel Obstruction (Mechanical and Functional/Ogilvie's Syndrome).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish mechanical from functional (Ogilvie's syndrome/colonic pseudo-obstruction) large bowel obstruction and identify appropriate initial investigation and management, including indications for decompression or surgery.
candidates.study_unit: Large Bowel Obstruction (Mechanical and Functional/Ogilvie's Syndrome)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply decontamination selection reasoning for Decontamination and Enhanced Elimination.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select appropriate decontamination method (activated charcoal, whole bowel irrigation, dermal/ocular irrigation) with attention to contraindications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply erythema nodosum reasoning for Angioedema, Urticaria, and Erythema Nodosum.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize erythema nodosum by tender, poorly-demarcated pretibial nodules and investigate for underlying causes (streptococcal infection, sarcoidosis, IBD, malignancy).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Sleep-Related Hypoventilation Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Treat reversible causes and refer for ventilatory support assessment when indicated.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply gonococcemia recognition reasoning for Cutaneous Manifestations of Sexually Transmitted Infections (Syphilis, Gonococcemia).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize disseminated gonococcal infection by hemorrhagic pustules on a purpuric background with arthritis/tenosynovitis, and initiate ceftriaxone with STI screening and public health notification.
candidates.study_unit: Cutaneous Manifestations of Sexually Transmitted Infections (Syphilis, Gonococcemia)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply mediastinal mass ddx reasoning for Mediastinal Masses.
candidates.source_competency_text: Localize a mediastinal mass by compartment (anterior, middle, posterior) and generate an appropriate differential diagnosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Recognition of Airspace and Parenchymal Lung Abnormalities (Atelectasis, Consolidation/Pneumonia, Pulmonary Nodule).
candidates.source_competency_text: Determine when a solitary pulmonary nodule requires further imaging (CT, PET/CT) versus Fleischner-guideline follow-up based on malignancy-risk features.
candidates.study_unit: Recognition of Airspace and Parenchymal Lung Abnormalities (Atelectasis, Consolidation/Pneumonia, Pulmonary Nodule)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Lymphedema.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the clinical features of lymphedema and identify when alternative or urgent causes of limb swelling require evaluation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Syncope and Loss of Consciousness (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify cardiac (arrhythmic, structural) vs. reflex vs. orthostatic causes.
candidates.study_unit: Syncope and Loss of Consciousness (Cardiac Differential)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply icp management reasoning for Treatment of Elevated ICP.
candidates.source_competency_text: State the stepwise conservative-to-aggressive management of elevated ICP (positioning, normocarbia, osmotic diuresis, sedation, CSF drainage, decompressive craniectomy).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply equity barriers reasoning for Equity in Palliative Care (Barriers to Access, Anti-Oppressive Care).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify patient/system characteristics associated with poorer access to palliative care (older age, race, unmarried/living alone, non-cancer diagnosis, sexual/gender minority status, homelessness, low socioeconomic status, long-term-care residence, rurality, disability, immigrant status) and the need to account for one's own biases in providing equitable palliative care.
candidates.study_unit: Equity in Palliative Care (Barriers to Access, Anti-Oppressive Care)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Malrotation of the Intestine (with Volvulus).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize bilious vomiting +/- abdominal distension/pain/hematochezia in an infant as malrotation with volvulus until proven otherwise, requiring emergent upper GI contrast study and surgical consultation to prevent bowel ischemia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigate reasoning for Systemic lupus erythematosus and Raynaud phenomenon.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify initial testing and organ-threatening features needing urgent referral.
candidates.study_unit: Systemic lupus erythematosus and Raynaud phenomenon

candidates.principal_decision: Apply wart recognition reasoning for Molluscum Contagiosum and Cutaneous HPV (Warts).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish verruca vulgaris, plantaris, and condyloma acuminata by site and morphology, and counsel on HPV subtypes associated with cervical/anogenital dysplasia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bcc recognition reasoning for Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers (Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Bowen's Disease).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize basal cell carcinoma by pearly, telangiectatic, rolled-border papule/nodule and select biopsy/excision as management.
candidates.study_unit: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers (Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Bowen's Disease)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stabilization reasoning for Disorders of Sexual Differentiation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize atypical genitalia with possible salt-wasting emergency and initiate urgent multidisciplinary assessment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Venous Thromboembolism: Diagnosis and Treatment.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate anticoagulation for confirmed VTE, recognize indications for thrombolysis in massive/submassive PE, and determine anticoagulation duration based on provoked vs. unprovoked status.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Duodenal Atresia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize duodenal atresia by the 'double bubble' sign on abdominal X-ray, bilious vomiting in the first day of life, and its association with Down syndrome.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Cyanosis in the Neonate.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use the hyperoxia test and clinical context to distinguish cardiac (cyanotic CHD -- minimal PaO2 rise with 100% O2) from pulmonary/other causes (PaO2 rises substantially with 100% O2) of neonatal cyanosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Depressive Disorders (Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder).
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) using DSM-5-type symptom/duration criteria and grade severity.
candidates.study_unit: Depressive Disorders (Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply immunization safety reasoning for Routine Immunization (Vaccine Schedule, Adverse Reactions, Contraindications).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish true contraindications to routine immunization (e.g. anaphylactic reaction to the vaccine or a component) from expected minor adverse reactions (fever, local soreness) that do not preclude future doses.
candidates.study_unit: Routine Immunization (Vaccine Schedule, Adverse Reactions, Contraindications)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Otalgia (Primary vs. Referred Ear Pain).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish primary otologic causes of ear pain (infection, trauma, cerumen, neoplasm) from referred pain via the sensory innervation of the ear (CN V, VII, IX, X), and recognize that a normal-appearing ear with persistent otalgia warrants a search for a referred source (dental, TMJ, pharyngeal/laryngeal malignancy, temporal arteritis).
candidates.study_unit: Approach to Otalgia (Primary vs. Referred Ear Pain)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Wilson's Disease and Dystonia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Wilson's disease (young patient with movement disorder/dystonia plus liver disease/Kayser-Fleischer rings) as a treatable, reversible cause of a movement disorder warranting screening (ceruloplasmin, copper studies).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply isotretinoin safety reasoning for Acne Vulgaris.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize isotretinoin's key safety requirements (pregnancy exclusion/contraception counselling, baseline lipid/LFT monitoring).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply confidence intervals reasoning for Statistical Hypothesis Testing, Error Types, and Confidence Intervals.
candidates.source_competency_text: Interpret a 95% confidence interval and explain how a wider interval reflects greater uncertainty for the same point estimate.
candidates.study_unit: Statistical Hypothesis Testing, Error Types, and Confidence Intervals

candidates.principal_decision: Apply sdh recognition reasoning for Subdural Hematoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the crescentic CT appearance of subdural hematoma and the higher-risk populations (elderly, anticoagulated, alcohol use) presenting subacutely/chronically.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply toxic megacolon recognition reasoning for Toxic Megacolon.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize toxic megacolon as a life-threatening complication of colitis (infectious or inflammatory) and initiate emergency management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply counselling reasoning for HIV Testing, Pre/Post-Test Counselling, and Prevention (PrEP/PEP).
candidates.source_competency_text: Provide appropriate pre- and post-test HIV counselling addressing stigma, risk assessment, and connection to support services.
candidates.study_unit: HIV Testing, Pre/Post-Test Counselling, and Prevention (PrEP/PEP)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply perineal trauma reasoning for Perineal Lacerations and Episiotomy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify perineal laceration degree and recognize indications for (and risks of) episiotomy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Illness Anxiety Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish illness anxiety disorder (preoccupation with having a serious illness, minimal/absent somatic symptoms, high health-related anxiety) from somatic symptom disorder (prominent somatic symptoms are the focus).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Pulmonary Embolism.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select and interpret D-dimer and imaging based on pretest probability and contraindications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate immediate ACS management (antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy, urgent reperfusion pathway activation).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply monitoring reasoning for Hypoxemic and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize deterioration and complications requiring critical-care referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply meconium recognition reasoning for Meconium (Meconium-Stained Amniotic Fluid).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize meconium-stained amniotic fluid intrapartum and its implication for delivery-room preparation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Orbital (Blow-Out) Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize enophthalmos, restricted upward gaze/vertical diplopia, and infraorbital numbness after blunt periorbital trauma as suggestive of orbital floor fracture, and recognize the 'white-eyed blow-out fracture' in children (muscle entrapment with minimal external signs) as a surgical emergency.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Vitreous Hemorrhage.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sudden painless vision loss with vitreous hemorrhage (diabetic retinopathy, retinal tear) as requiring urgent ophthalmology referral to identify and treat the underlying cause.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply etiologic assessment reasoning for General Approach to Interstitial Lung Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Elicit connective-tissue, occupational, environmental, medication, and treatment exposures and select initial investigations.
candidates.study_unit: General Approach to Interstitial Lung Disease

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate an appropriate management plan (conservative vs. pessary vs. surgical referral).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply epidemiology triad reasoning for Communicable Disease Control and Infection Prevention and Control Practices.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the host-agent-environment epidemiology triad framework to identify a communicable-disease control intervention target.
candidates.study_unit: Communicable Disease Control and Infection Prevention and Control Practices

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Supracondylar Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize supracondylar fracture as the most common pediatric elbow fracture and the classic cause of brachial artery injury and compartment syndrome (Volkmann's ischemic contracture); perform and document a careful neurovascular exam (radial pulse, AIN/median nerve function) before and after any splinting.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply tinea site recognition reasoning for Dermatophyte Infections (Tinea Capitis, Corporis, Cruris, Pedis, Manuum, Unguium, Barbae).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the site-specific presentations of dermatophyte infection (tinea capitis with kerion, corporis, cruris, pedis, unguium) and select topical vs. oral antifungal therapy based on site and severity.
candidates.study_unit: Dermatophyte Infections (Tinea Capitis, Corporis, Cruris, Pedis, Manuum, Unguium, Barbae)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply measures of effect reasoning for Effectiveness of Interventions and Measures of Effect (RR, OR, AR, NNT, NNH).
candidates.source_competency_text: Calculate odds ratio (case-control) and relative risk/attributable risk (cohort) from a 2x2 exposure-disease table.
candidates.study_unit: Effectiveness of Interventions and Measures of Effect (RR, OR, AR, NNT, NNH)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Syphilis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose staged syphilis (primary/secondary/latent/tertiary/neurosyphilis) using the Public-Health-Lab serology algorithm and recognize congenital syphilis stigmata.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Indications for Referral to a Burn Centre.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize burn characteristics (TBSA threshold, depth, special-site involvement, inhalation injury, patient factors) that mandate transfer to a specialized burn centre.
candidates.study_unit: Indications for Referral to a Burn Centre

candidates.principal_decision: Apply melanoma risk reasoning for Malignant Melanoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize risk factors and monitoring requirements for melanoma (atypical/dysplastic nevi, family history, UV exposure).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Children (incl. Obstructive Sleep Apnea).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize snoring, witnessed apneic pauses, restless sleep, and daytime behavioural/learning problems as pediatric sleep-disordered breathing, most commonly due to adenotonsillar hypertrophy, and know adenotonsillectomy is first-line treatment when hypertrophy is the cause.
candidates.study_unit: Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Children (incl. Obstructive Sleep Apnea)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply celiac diagnosis reasoning for Celiac Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose celiac disease via serology and duodenal biopsy in a patient with chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, iron-deficiency anemia, or abnormal liver enzymes, and initiate gluten-free diet management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Carotid Stenosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize carotid disease in the TIA/stroke risk context and perform an appropriate focused examination.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Sleep-Related Hypoventilation Syndromes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess daytime hypercapnia, oxygenation, medication contributors, and need for formal sleep or respiratory testing.
