candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize ECT has no absolute contraindications and that its most clinically significant adverse effect is memory loss, which is usually transient.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply legal professional action reasoning for Negligence.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize a potential negligence/standard-of-care concern and determine appropriate next steps.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Bradyarrhythmias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize symptomatic bradyarrhythmia (sinus node dysfunction, AV block) on ECG.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply o2 delivery reasoning for Oxygen Therapy and Mechanical Ventilation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Match oxygen delivery method to patient status (intubated vs. spontaneously breathing) and target SaO2 >90%.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Pediatric Dysrhythmias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize supraventricular tachycardia as the most common pediatric dysrhythmia (narrow-complex, rate typically >220 bpm in infants) and the initial management sequence (vagal maneuvers, adenosine, synchronized cardioversion if unstable).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Rotator Cuff Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize rotator cuff impingement/tear on history (painful arc, night pain) and exam (empty can, drop-arm test) and know initial non-operative management versus indications for surgical referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply planning cycles reasoning for Quality Improvement Concepts and Systems Analysis Tools.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle or the Precede-Proceed model to design and evaluate a health intervention.
candidates.study_unit: Quality Improvement Concepts and Systems Analysis Tools

candidates.principal_decision: Apply risk stratification reasoning for Suicide Risk Assessment and Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Stratify suicide risk using SAD PERSONS-type factors (demographics, psychiatric/substance comorbidity, past attempts, access to means, protective factors) and distinguish passive from active ideation with plan/intent.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply universal antidotes reasoning for Approach to the Overdose/Poisoned Patient (History, Primary/Secondary Survey, Universal Antidotes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Administer universal empiric antidotes (naloxone, dextrose) in suspected overdose.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to the Overdose/Poisoned Patient (History, Primary/Secondary Survey, Universal Antidotes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Oppositional Defiant Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose ODD (pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behaviour, or vindictiveness for >=6 mo) and recognize disruptive mood dysregulation disorder supersedes ODD when both are met.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply screening selection reasoning for Prenatal Screening and Diagnostic Tests.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select and interpret appropriate prenatal screening and diagnostic tests by trimester and risk profile, and counsel on their voluntary nature.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Differential Diagnosis of Common Respiratory Presentations.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize unstable or life-threatening respiratory presentations and prioritize immediate assessment.
candidates.study_unit: Differential Diagnosis of Common Respiratory Presentations

candidates.principal_decision: Apply triage reasoning for Approach to and General Management of Traumatic Hand Injuries.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish injuries requiring emergent OR exploration from those suitable for delayed/outpatient management.
candidates.study_unit: Approach to and General Management of Traumatic Hand Injuries

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial action reasoning for Peripheral Arterial Disease and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Perform a basic vascular examination, use initial non-invasive investigation appropriately, address risk factors, and identify when urgent vascular assessment is needed.
candidates.study_unit: Peripheral Arterial Disease and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Pediatric Brain Tumours.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize raised-ICP red flags for pediatric brain tumour (early-morning headache/vomiting, ataxia, cranial nerve palsies, papilledema) prompting urgent neuroimaging, given posterior fossa tumours are the most common pediatric solid tumour location.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition and management reasoning for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize PID from its clinical presentation (pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness, discharge, fever), initiate empiric antibiotic treatment, and identify indications for hospitalization or drainage of tubo-ovarian abscess.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ethical reasoning reasoning for Indigenous Health Disparities and Comorbidities.
candidates.source_competency_text: Provide anti-racist, culturally safe, trauma-informed care.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis and management reasoning for Atrial Septal Defect (ASD).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the three ASD subtypes (ostium primum -- associated with Down syndrome; ostium secundum -- most common; sinus venosus), the fixed-split-S2 exam finding, and the high spontaneous-closure rate for small defects vs. elective closure for larger ones.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply headache red flags reasoning for Headache (ED Approach, incl. Meningitis Red Flags).
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify red-flag features (thunderclap onset, fever/neck stiffness, focal deficit, papilledema) requiring urgent headache workup.
candidates.study_unit: Headache (ED Approach, incl. Meningitis Red Flags)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply infectious colitis recognition reasoning for Infectious Colitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize infectious colitis (including C. difficile) as a cause of acute/bloody diarrhea and lower GI bleeding, and initiate appropriate testing and treatment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis management reasoning for Otitis Externa.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize otitis externa by pain on tragal traction/pinna manipulation with EAC edema and erythema, initiate topical antimicrobial therapy (avoiding ototoxic agents such as gentamicin or neomycin if the TM is perforated or status is unknown), and recognize risk factors (water exposure, instrumentation, diabetes).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply therapeutic index reasoning for Pharmacodynamics: Dose-Response, Efficacy, Potency, and Therapeutic Index.
candidates.source_competency_text: Calculate/interpret the Therapeutic Index (TD50/ED50 or LD50/ED50) and apply the principle that a larger TI indicates a safer drug; recognize the named narrow-TI drugs that commonly require TDM (digoxin, theophylline, warfarin, lithium, cyclosporine).
candidates.study_unit: Pharmacodynamics: Dose-Response, Efficacy, Potency, and Therapeutic Index

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Acute Confusional State / Delirium.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize delirium (acute onset, fluctuating course, altered level of consciousness/attention), differentiate it from dementia and psychiatric disorders, identify the underlying cause, and initiate urgent management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Language Delay.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate expressive/receptive language delay from isolated speech-sound (articulation) disorder, and recognize red flags (regression, no words by 18 mo, no phrases by 2 yr) warranting audiology and formal assessment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Pulmonary Vasculitis and Alveolar Hemorrhage.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pulmonary-renal, upper-airway, eosinophilic, or diffuse-alveolar-hemorrhage patterns suggesting systemic vasculitis or anti-GBM disease.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply angiodysplasia recognition reasoning for Angiodysplasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize angiodysplasia as a vascular cause of lower GI bleeding, particularly in older adults.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bariatric indications reasoning for Bariatric Surgery.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize general indications for bariatric surgery and major postoperative complications (e.g., anastomotic leak, nutritional deficiency, dumping syndrome).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Aplastic Anemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize aplastic anemia (pancytopenia with hypocellular bone marrow) and identify major causes (idiopathic autoimmune, drug/toxin, viral, inherited).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply definitional distinction reasoning for Paraphilic Disorders.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that a paraphilia becomes a paraphilic disorder only when it causes distress/impairment to the individual or entails harm/risk of harm to others, without needing forensic-psychiatry-level classification detail.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention reasoning for Travel Medicine (General Travel Precautions, Fever in the Returned Traveller).
candidates.source_competency_text: Advise on pre-travel vaccination, malaria chemoprophylaxis, and food/water precautions.
candidates.study_unit: Travel Medicine (General Travel Precautions, Fever in the Returned Traveller)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply medical instability reasoning for Anorexia Nervosa.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize signs of medical instability (bradycardia, hypotension, electrolyte disturbance, arrhythmia risk) requiring urgent medical stabilization/hospitalization, and the risk of refeeding syndrome when nutritional rehabilitation begins.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply acne grading reasoning for Acne Vulgaris.
candidates.source_competency_text: Grade acne severity (comedonal to nodulocystic) and select first-line topical versus systemic therapy accordingly.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Pneumothorax and Tension Pneumothorax.
candidates.source_competency_text: Use appropriate imaging for stable suspected pneumothorax and recognize complications.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize a typical IPF presentation and usual interstitial pneumonia pattern at a generalist level.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Thrombocytopenia (Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Generate a differential for thrombocytopenia (decreased production, increased destruction/consumption, sequestration) and recognize features requiring urgent workup (e.g., microangiopathic hemolysis, active bleeding).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Generalized Edema.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select investigations to establish the mechanism (e.g., BNP, echocardiogram, renal/liver panel).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply extubation readiness reasoning for General Anesthesia Maintenance and Extubation Readiness.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the four extubation-readiness criteria (no intubation requirement, patent airway, intact reflexes, adequate spontaneous ventilation) before extubating a patient.
candidates.study_unit: General Anesthesia Maintenance and Extubation Readiness

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Pelvic Mass.
candidates.source_competency_text: Generate a differential for a pelvic mass by patient age/menopausal status and characterize features (size, laterality, mobility, associated findings) suggesting malignancy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stabilization reasoning for Acute Care and Initial Resuscitation of Burn Patients.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply primary-survey (ABCs) principles to a major burn patient, recognize airway-compromise risk from inhalation injury, and understand that fluid resuscitation is guided by TBSA and weight-based formulas.
candidates.study_unit: Acute Care and Initial Resuscitation of Burn Patients

candidates.principal_decision: Apply clinical examples reasoning for Drug-Receptor Interactions: Agonists and Antagonists.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the agonist/antagonist framework to named clinical examples (naloxone as a reversible competitive antagonist at opioid receptors; buprenorphine as a partial mu-opioid agonist).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply chest pain primary care reasoning for Chest Pain.
candidates.source_competency_text: Evaluate chest pain in the primary-care/outpatient setting, with particular attention to excluding life-threatening causes requiring urgent referral versus musculoskeletal/GI causes manageable longitudinally.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Nasal Fractures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize nasal fracture and, critically, identify septal hematoma requiring urgent drainage to prevent cartilage necrosis/saddle-nose deformity.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Pulmonary Hypertension.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pulmonary hypertension from progressive dyspnea, exertional syncope, right-heart findings, and suggestive tests.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply disposition reasoning for Pulmonary Embolism.
candidates.source_competency_text: Risk-stratify confirmed PE and identify patients requiring admission versus potential outpatient care.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Erectile Dysfunction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess erectile dysfunction, contributing disease and medication risk, and provide initial support/referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, and Factor XI Deficiency.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize factor replacement as the mainstay of acute bleed management and prophylaxis.
candidates.study_unit: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, and Factor XI Deficiency

candidates.principal_decision: Apply thymoma recognition reasoning for Thymoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize thymoma as the classic anterior mediastinal mass and its association with myasthenia gravis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hazard classification reasoning for Environmental Health Framework, Jurisdiction, and Risk Assessment.
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify an environmental exposure into its hazard category (chemical, biological, physical, radiation) and reservoir (air, water, soil, food).
candidates.study_unit: Environmental Health Framework, Jurisdiction, and Risk Assessment

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Chronic Venous Insufficiency.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize chronic venous disease features and complications such as venous ulceration, and distinguish them from ischemic-wound context.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Duchenne muscular dystrophy presenting with proximal muscle weakness, positive Gowers' sign, and calf pseudohypertrophy in a young boy, and identify creatine kinase elevation and molecular testing as the diagnostic approach.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Pediatric Seizures (General Management, Seizure Mimics).
candidates.source_competency_text: Work up a first unprovoked seizure (electrolytes, glucose, EEG, neuroimaging if indicated) while excluding seizure mimics (breath-holding spells, syncope, night terrors, non-epileptic/pseudoseizure, TIA, tics), and apply general antiepileptic-therapy initiation principles (treat after 2+ unprovoked afebrile seizures, single-drug optimization before combination therapy).
candidates.study_unit: Approach to Pediatric Seizures (General Management, Seizure Mimics)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply nail systemic association reasoning for Nail Disorders and Primary Hyperhidrosis (Adnexal Disorders).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize nail changes (e.g., pitting, onycholysis, yellow nail syndrome) as cutaneous markers of an underlying systemic or dermatologic condition using Table 24.
candidates.study_unit: Nail Disorders and Primary Hyperhidrosis (Adnexal Disorders)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Ankle Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize ankle fracture patterns (Danis-Weber/Lauge-Hansen classification concepts), apply the Ottawa Ankle Rules to guide imaging, and know unstable/displaced fractures require operative fixation while stable fractures may be managed with casting.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Meniscal Tears.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize meniscal tear (joint-line tenderness, mechanical locking/catching, positive McMurray's) and know a truly locked knee (fixed extension block) is a surgical emergency.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Potassium Disorders: Hyperkalemia and Hypokalemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of hyperkalemia and hypokalemia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply syncope risk stratify reasoning for Syncope (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate cardiogenic (high-risk) from non-cardiogenic causes of syncope and risk-stratify for admission.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply workup reasoning for Uterine (Endometrial) Cancer.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate appropriate first-line investigation (endometrial biopsy/imaging) and recognize indications for urgent gynecologic-oncology referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Sleep Disorders (Overview, Insomnia, Sleep Apnea, Restless Legs Syndrome, Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, Narcolepsy, Parasomnias).
candidates.source_competency_text: Take a sleep history to differentiate insomnia, sleep apnea, RLS/PLMD, narcolepsy, and parasomnias, screen for safety concerns (e.g., excessive daytime somnolence and driving), and determine when polysomnography or specialized referral is required.
candidates.study_unit: Sleep Disorders (Overview, Insomnia, Sleep Apnea, Restless Legs Syndrome, Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, Narcolepsy, Parasomnias)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Constrictive Pericarditis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate constrictive pericarditis from restrictive cardiomyopathy conceptually.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bph reasoning for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose BPH from a lower-urinary-tract-symptom presentation, exclude red-flag features (e.g., suspected malignancy, retention), and initiate first-line medical management (alpha-blocker, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stabilization reasoning for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Obstruction.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize retention/obstruction, obtain initial investigations, decompress when indicated and escalate complications.
candidates.study_unit: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Obstruction

candidates.principal_decision: Apply koh prep reasoning for Dermatophyte Infections (Tinea Capitis, Corporis, Cruris, Pedis, Manuum, Unguium, Barbae).
candidates.source_competency_text: Use KOH preparation of skin scrapings as the confirmatory investigation for suspected dermatophyte infection.
candidates.study_unit: Dermatophyte Infections (Tinea Capitis, Corporis, Cruris, Pedis, Manuum, Unguium, Barbae)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply visit schedule reasoning for Well-Child Visit Overview (Approach to the Pediatric History and Periodic Health Encounter).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the periodic well-child visit schedule as the structural backbone for growth, development, immunization, and anticipatory-guidance surveillance.
candidates.study_unit: Well-Child Visit Overview (Approach to the Pediatric History and Periodic Health Encounter)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize monomorphic/polymorphic VT on ECG and distinguish from SVT with aberrancy.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply uterine inversion recognition reasoning for Uterine Inversion.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize uterine inversion (fundus not palpable abdominally, hemorrhage, shock) and initiate emergency management (manual replacement, resuscitation).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply anatomic differences reasoning for Pediatric Anesthesia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize pediatric airway anatomic differences (large head/tongue, short trachea, superior/anterior larynx) that alter airway management technique vs. adults.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Maxillary (Le Fort) Fractures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize features of midface instability (Le Fort pattern) and the airway/CSF-leak risks that mandate urgent evaluation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Chronic Kidney Disease: KDIGO Staging, Complications, and Management.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose and stage CKD using GFR category and albuminuria (KDIGO 2024 criteria) and identify the underlying cause.
candidates.study_unit: Chronic Kidney Disease: KDIGO Staging, Complications, and Management

candidates.principal_decision: Apply historical context reasoning for Indigenous Health in Canada and the Legacy of Colonization.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify the major historical mechanisms of colonial harm to Indigenous health in Canada (residential schools, coercive nutrition research, forced relocation to TB sanatoriums, coerced sterilization, the Sixties Scoop) and their documented intergenerational health effects.
candidates.study_unit: Indigenous Health in Canada and the Legacy of Colonization

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) Deficiency.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize X-linked G6PD deficiency presenting as episodic hemolysis triggered by oxidative stress (drugs, infection, fava beans), with Heinz bodies and bite cells on blood film.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply screening vs diagnosis reasoning for Screening Principles and Screening Biases.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish the purpose of a screening test (detect early disease/risk in asymptomatic people) from a diagnostic test (confirm disease in symptomatic/screen-positive people).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply imaging decision reasoning for Neurotrauma: Trauma Assessment and Head/Brain Injury.
candidates.source_competency_text: State indications for urgent CT head after trauma.
candidates.study_unit: Neurotrauma: Trauma Assessment and Head/Brain Injury

candidates.principal_decision: Apply alopecia ddx reasoning for Alopecia (Non-Scarring and Scarring) and Hypertrichosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish non-scarring alopecia (telogen/anagen effluvium, alopecia areata, androgenic alopecia) from scarring alopecia by history, distribution, and follicular ostia preservation, and recognize scarring alopecia as requiring biopsy/dermatology referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply grief recognition reasoning for Types of Grief (Anticipatory, Acute, Complicated).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish normal anticipatory/acute grief from complicated grief (prolonged duration, maladaptive thoughts, dysregulated emotions, dysfunctional behaviours, with prevalent comorbid depression/anxiety) as a trigger for additional support or referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Gastroesophageal Reflux (Infant).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish physiologic GER ('happy spitter', normal growth) from pathologic GERD (FTT, esophagitis, respiratory complications) requiring further workup/treatment.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ibs diagnosis reasoning for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose IBS as a functional motility disorder using symptom-based criteria after excluding organic disease, in a patient with chronic abdominal pain, altered bowel habits, or constipation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply respiratory manifestations reasoning for Cystic Fibrosis (Respiratory/Pulmonary Manifestations).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize CF's respiratory manifestations (recurrent/chronic respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, declining lung function), the role of sweat chloride testing and CFTR mutation analysis in diagnosis, and chest-disease management principles (airway clearance physiotherapy, mucolytics, antibiotics targeted by sputum culture).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply procedure reasoning for Lumbar Puncture.
candidates.source_competency_text: State indications, contraindications, and interpretation basics of lumbar puncture (opening pressure, CSF analysis) as used in the headache, coma, and CNS-infection diagnostic pathways.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Thrombotic Microangiopathies (TTP/HUS).
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate urgent plasma exchange for suspected TTP without delaying for confirmatory testing, and recognize that platelet transfusion is generally contraindicated.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Numbness/Altered Sensation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a patient with numbness/tingling, take a history and perform an exam aimed at the underlying cause (e.g., diabetic, compressive, demyelinating) and construct an initial management/referral plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose GAD (excessive worry >=6 mo, difficult to control, with associated symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, concentration difficulty, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance) and grade severity/functional impact.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Motor Neuron Disease: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize combined upper and lower motor neuron signs without sensory involvement as characteristic of ALS, outline the EMG/NCS and imaging workup used to support the diagnosis, and describe disease-modifying (riluzole) vs. supportive management.
candidates.study_unit: Motor Neuron Disease: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial management reasoning for Infective Endocarditis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications for antibiotic prophylaxis in at-risk patients undergoing procedures.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Cryptorchidism and Ectopic Testes.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize undescended/ectopic testes and arrange appropriate referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Antidiuretic Hormone Disorders (Diabetes Insipidus, SIADH).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate SIADH (euvolemic hyponatremia, concentrated urine) from diabetes insipidus (polyuria, dilute urine despite hypernatremia/dehydration) and recognize their respective common pediatric causes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply vitiligo workup reasoning for Vitiligo.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize vitiligo (depigmented macules, Wood's lamp confirmation) and screen for associated autoimmune disease (thyroid disease, T1DM, Addison's, pernicious anemia).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Approach to Weakness.
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a patient with weakness, differentiate true weakness from fatigue/pain/inhibition, localize to muscle/peripheral nerve/UMN pathway, and determine the most likely underlying cause and initial workup.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for End-Stage Renal Disease: Definition, Risk Factors, and Uremic Presentation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the multi-system presentation of uremic syndrome (volume overload, electrolyte abnormalities, cognitive/GI/hematologic/endocrine manifestations) as an indication for renal replacement therapy.
candidates.study_unit: End-Stage Renal Disease: Definition, Risk Factors, and Uremic Presentation

candidates.principal_decision: Apply polypharmacy recognition reasoning for Polypharmacy and Inappropriate Prescribing in Older Adults.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize polypharmacy and potentially inappropriate medications as a contributing cause of falls, delirium, and other geriatric syndromes covered elsewhere in this chapter.
candidates.study_unit: Polypharmacy and Inappropriate Prescribing in Older Adults

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Somatic Symptom Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that regular scheduled follow-up (not symptom-contingent visits) and avoiding unnecessary investigations are key management principles.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply labour analgesia options reasoning for Analgesic and Anesthetic Techniques in Labour and Birth.
candidates.source_competency_text: Discuss available analgesic/anesthetic options in labour (neuraxial, systemic, non-pharmacologic) and their major contraindications with a patient.
candidates.study_unit: Analgesic and Anesthetic Techniques in Labour and Birth

candidates.principal_decision: Apply mitigation vs adaptation reasoning for Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Public Health Response.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish mitigation (reducing emissions to slow climate change) from adaptation (preparing health systems for climate change's effects).
candidates.study_unit: Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Public Health Response

candidates.principal_decision: Apply psoriasis severity management reasoning for Psoriasis (Plaque, Guttate, Erythrodermic, Pustular, Inverse) and Systemic Therapy.
candidates.source_competency_text: Select management by disease severity (BSA/PASI): topical therapy for mild disease, phototherapy or systemic/biologic therapy for moderate-severe disease; recognize erythrodermic and generalized pustular psoriasis as potentially life-threatening requiring urgent management.
candidates.study_unit: Psoriasis (Plaque, Guttate, Erythrodermic, Pustular, Inverse) and Systemic Therapy

candidates.principal_decision: Apply crohns surgical reasoning for Crohn's Disease (Surgical Indications and Management).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize indications for surgery in Crohn's disease (stricture, fistula, abscess, failure of medical therapy) and general operative principles (bowel-sparing resection).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply abdo pain triage reasoning for Acute Abdominal Pain (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate emergent (surgical/vascular) from less-emergent causes of acute abdominal pain in the ED.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply emergency reasoning for Retinal Detachment.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the flashes/floaters/curtain-field-loss triad as retinal detachment requiring same-day ophthalmology referral, and distinguish rhegmatogenous from other detachment types.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for von Willebrand Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize vWD presenting with mucocutaneous bleeding and a prolonged PTT with normal PT, confirmed by vWF antigen/activity and factor VIII level.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply assessment reasoning for Consent and Capacity.
candidates.source_competency_text: Assess decision-making capacity for a specific decision.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply counselling reasoning for Routine Immunization (Vaccine Schedule, Adverse Reactions, Contraindications).
candidates.source_competency_text: Counsel caregivers on the routine immunization schedule and address common vaccine-hesitancy concerns.
candidates.study_unit: Routine Immunization (Vaccine Schedule, Adverse Reactions, Contraindications)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ich recognition reasoning for Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize intracerebral hemorrhage on NCCT and the indications for urgent neurosurgical consultation (deterioration, mass effect, cerebellar hemorrhage).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential reasoning for Dyspnea (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate cardiac from pulmonary and other causes of dyspnea.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention reasoning for Noise-Induced Sensorineural Hearing Loss.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize occupational/recreational high-volume noise exposure as a cause of bilateral high-frequency (classically 4000 Hz notch) SNHL and counsel on hearing protection as primary prevention.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Cardiac Infections (Infective Endocarditis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize infective endocarditis in a patient with new/changing murmur, fever, and risk factors (IVDU, prosthetic valve, prior IE).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply code status reasoning for End-of-Life Decision Making (Advance Care Planning, Goals of Care, Code Status).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish full code, DNR/comfort measures, and Allow Natural Death (AND) terminology, and recognize that CPR is rarely effective and a DNR order is almost always consistent with palliative goals of care in advanced incurable illness.
candidates.study_unit: End-of-Life Decision Making (Advance Care Planning, Goals of Care, Code Status)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ethical reasoning reasoning for History and Impact of Colonialism, and the Movement Towards Reconciliation.
candidates.source_competency_text: Articulate how colonialism's historical impact and the TRC's Calls to Action inform current clinical and system-level practice.
candidates.study_unit: History and Impact of Colonialism, and the Movement Towards Reconciliation

candidates.principal_decision: Apply classification reasoning for Anemia (Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify anemia by MCV (microcytic/normocytic/macrocytic) and reticulocyte-response as the entry point to the specific-diagnosis units below.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply stabilization reasoning for Acute Scrotal Pain and Scrotal Mass.
candidates.source_competency_text: Treat acute scrotal pain as torsion until excluded and distinguish mass presentations requiring urgent referral.
candidates.study_unit: Acute Scrotal Pain and Scrotal Mass

candidates.principal_decision: Apply benign growth recognition reasoning for Benign Fibrous and Hyperkeratotic Skin Lesions (Dermatofibroma, Skin Tags, Seborrheic Keratosis, Corns, Keloids).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize common benign skin growths (dermatofibroma, skin tag, seborrheic keratosis, corn, keloid) by characteristic clinical features and distinguish them from premalignant/malignant mimics (e.g., Leser-Trelat sign as a paraneoplastic clue).
candidates.study_unit: Benign Fibrous and Hyperkeratotic Skin Lesions (Dermatofibroma, Skin Tags, Seborrheic Keratosis, Corns, Keloids)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Pelvic Fracture.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize unstable pelvic fracture (mechanism, pelvic instability on exam -- performed only once, gently) as a hemorrhage-risk emergency requiring pelvic binder, resuscitation, and urgent orthopedic/trauma team involvement.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Polycythemia Vera.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose PV using JAK2 mutation testing and diagnostic criteria, distinguishing it from secondary/spurious erythrocytosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply reporting reasoning for Adverse Drug Reactions: Classification and Clinical Approach.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize which suspected ADRs require formal reporting (unexpected, serious, or reactions to drugs on the market <5 years) and the Canadian reporting pathway (MedEffect Canada / Canada Vigilance).
candidates.study_unit: Adverse Drug Reactions: Classification and Clinical Approach

candidates.principal_decision: Apply gastritis recognition reasoning for Gastritis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize gastritis as a cause of upper abdominal pain and/or upper GI bleeding and identify common etiologies (H. pylori, NSAIDs, alcohol).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply localization reasoning for Cranial Nerve Deficits (CN I-XII Localizing Syndromes).
candidates.source_competency_text: Given a described deficit pattern (e.g., ptosis with a 'down and out' eye, facial droop sparing the forehead, hoarseness with dysphagia), identify the cranial nerve involved and the most likely level/cause of the lesion.
candidates.study_unit: Cranial Nerve Deficits (CN I-XII Localizing Syndromes)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Early Pregnancy Loss and First-Trimester Bleeding.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate appropriate management (expectant, medical, or surgical) and provide supportive counselling; investigate recurrent pregnancy loss.
candidates.study_unit: Early Pregnancy Loss and First-Trimester Bleeding

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hiatus hernia recognition reasoning for Hiatus Hernia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sliding vs. paraesophageal hiatus hernia and identify indications for surgical repair (e.g., paraesophageal hernia with volvulus risk).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply shock ddx reasoning for Intraoperative Hypotension and Shock.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate intraoperative shock etiologies (septic, spinal/neurogenic, hypovolemic/hemorrhagic, obstructive) by their distinguishing hemodynamic pattern (e.g., warm skin without tachycardia in neurogenic shock).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Potassium Disorders: Hyperkalemia and Hypokalemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate emergency treatment for hyperkalemia (calcium stabilization, insulin/glucose, shift/elimination therapies) and appropriate repletion for hypokalemia.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply crohns recognition reasoning for Crohn's Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the distinguishing features of Crohn's disease (skip lesions, transmural inflammation, any GI segment, fistulizing/stricturing complications) and initiate an appropriate diagnostic/management plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply hyperandrogenism workup reasoning for Hyperandrogenism.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish adrenal from ovarian sources of hyperandrogenism/hirsutism using DHEAS and testosterone levels, and recognize red-flag features suggesting an androgen-secreting tumour.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pud surgical complications reasoning for Peptic Ulcer Disease (Surgical Complications).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize perforated and bleeding peptic ulcer as surgical emergencies and identify indications for operative vs. endoscopic/medical management.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Dislocated Knee (Tibiofemoral Dislocation).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize true knee dislocation as a limb-threatening emergency requiring urgent assessment for popliteal artery injury (ABI, +/- angiography) and peroneal nerve injury, even after spontaneous reduction.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply initial visit reasoning for Initial Prenatal Visit.
candidates.source_competency_text: Perform and interpret the components of an initial prenatal visit, including baseline history, physical exam, and first-trimester investigations.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Sickle Cell Disease.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize sickle cell disease genotypes (HbSS, HbSC, HbS-beta-thal) and their chronic manifestations (hemolytic anemia, functional asplenia/infection risk, growth delay).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply occupational vs nonoccupational reasoning for Occupational Medicine Overview and Occupational History Taking.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that occupational disease often looks clinically identical to non-occupational disease and may go unrecognized without a deliberate occupational history.
candidates.study_unit: Occupational Medicine Overview and Occupational History Taking

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease (Coxa Plana).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize Legg-Calve-Perthes disease as a cause of insidious hip pain/limp in a young child (peak age 4-10, boys) distinct from SCFE (older, obese adolescent) and transient synovitis (acute, post-viral), requiring x-ray and orthopedic referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply decision rule reasoning for Evaluation of Ankle and Foot Complaints.
candidates.source_competency_text: Apply the Ottawa Ankle and Foot Rules to determine the need for x-ray after acute ankle/foot injury, and perform anterior drawer/talar tilt tests to assess ligamentous stability.
candidates.study_unit: Evaluation of Ankle and Foot Complaints

candidates.principal_decision: Apply manage reasoning for Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome.
candidates.source_competency_text: Arrange urgent appropriate specialty and obstetric/hematology collaboration when indicated.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply complications reasoning for Renal Replacement Therapy: Dialysis Modalities, Indications, and Complications.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize dialysis-associated complications (disequilibrium syndrome, catheter-related infection/bacteremia, hemodynamic instability).
candidates.study_unit: Renal Replacement Therapy: Dialysis Modalities, Indications, and Complications

candidates.principal_decision: Apply bp vs pv reasoning for Bullous Pemphigoid.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish bullous pemphigoid (deeper, tense bullae) from pemphigus vulgaris (superficial, flaccid bullae, mucosal involvement, positive Nikolsky sign).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply uc recognition reasoning for Ulcerative Colitis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the distinguishing features of ulcerative colitis (continuous colonic/rectal involvement, mucosal inflammation, bloody diarrhea) and initiate an appropriate diagnostic/management plan.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate first-line management (exposure and response prevention CBT and/or SSRI at OCD-specific higher dosing) and recognize refractory-disease escalation options exist without needing procedural detail.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply acs initial mgmt reasoning for Acute Coronary Syndrome (ED Approach).
candidates.source_competency_text: Initiate first-line ACS management (ASA, anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy) in the ED.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply management reasoning for Open Fractures.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize an open fracture as a surgical emergency, apply emergency measures (sterile dressing, splint, IV antibiotics by Gustilo grade, tetanus status, urgent OR for debridement within 6-8 h), and avoid premature wound exploration in the field/ED.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply approach reasoning for Constipation (Pediatric).
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish functional constipation (the overwhelming majority) from organic red flags (delayed meconium passage >48h suggesting Hirschsprung disease, ribbon stools, FTT) and outline first-line management (disimpaction, maintenance osmotic laxative, behavioural toileting strategies).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differential and red flags reasoning for Crying/Fussy Infant (and Infantile Colic).
candidates.source_competency_text: Work through the crying/fussy-infant differential systematically (feeding/behavioural, infectious, physical injury including hair tourniquet and non-accidental trauma, medication/vaccine reaction, neonatal withdrawal) and recognize that infantile colic is a diagnosis of exclusion in an otherwise well, thriving infant.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply pv management reasoning for Pemphigus Vulgaris and Pemphigus Foliaceus.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize that pemphigus vulgaris requires prompt systemic immunosuppression and can be fatal if untreated, unlike the generally self-limited course of most other vesiculobullous rashes.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply adhf recognition reasoning for Heart Failure (Acute Decompensated).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize left- and right-sided heart failure presentations and identify precipitants of acute decompensation.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention followup reasoning for Rheumatic Fever.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize the rationale for secondary antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent recurrence and valve damage.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply biotransformation reasoning for Drug Metabolism and Cytochrome P450-Mediated Interactions.
candidates.source_competency_text: Classify a drug-metabolism pathway as phase I (oxidation/reduction/hydrolysis, often CYP-mediated) or phase II (conjugation) and predict the consequence (activation of a prodrug, formation of a toxic metabolite, inactivation).
candidates.study_unit: Drug Metabolism and Cytochrome P450-Mediated Interactions

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diagnosis reasoning for Intermittent Explosive Disorder.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize intermittent explosive disorder (recurrent impulsive-aggressive outbursts grossly out of proportion to precipitating stressors) and that it can be diagnosed alongside ADHD/CD/ODD/ASD when outbursts exceed what those diagnoses typically explain.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply prevention counselling reasoning for Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS).
candidates.source_competency_text: Counsel every caregiver on modifiable SIDS risk-reduction factors (supine sleep positioning, firm sleep surface, room-sharing without bed-sharing, avoidance of soft bedding/overheating, smoke-exposure avoidance).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply communication reasoning for Truth-Telling.
candidates.source_competency_text: Honestly and accurately disclose information, including medical error, to patients and families.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply thyrotoxicosis ddx reasoning for Thyrotoxicosis: Overview and Differential Diagnosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Generate a differential diagnosis for thyrotoxicosis (Graves', toxic adenoma/MNG, subacute thyroiditis, exogenous thyroid hormone) using clinical features and radioactive iodine uptake.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply recognition reasoning for Bone and Joint Infections (Septic Arthritis, Diabetic Foot Infections, Osteomyelitis).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize septic arthritis as a medical emergency requiring urgent joint aspiration and empiric antibiotics before joint destruction occurs.
candidates.study_unit: Bone and Joint Infections (Septic Arthritis, Diabetic Foot Infections, Osteomyelitis)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply diverticulosis recognition reasoning for Diverticulosis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize diverticulosis as the most common cause of acute lower GI bleeding and distinguish it from diverticulitis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply candidal intertrigo reasoning for Superficial Yeast Infections (Candidiasis, Tinea Versicolor).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize candidal intertrigo by satellite pustules in skin folds and identify predisposing factors (obesity, diabetes, antibiotics, immunosuppression).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply red flags reasoning for Mastoiditis.
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize postauricular erythema, tenderness, and a protruding/displaced auricle following acute otitis media as mastoiditis, requiring urgent imaging (CT) and IV antibiotics +/- mastoidectomy given the risk of intracranial extension.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply differentiation reasoning for Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.
candidates.source_competency_text: Distinguish Hodgkin lymphoma (bimodal age distribution, contiguous spread, Reed-Sternberg cells) from non-Hodgkin lymphoma (broader age range, non-contiguous spread, heterogeneous subtypes) at a recognition level.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply abdominal pain reasoning for Abdominal Pain.
candidates.source_competency_text: Undertake an undifferentiated primary-care assessment of a patient with abdominal pain, distinguishing benign/self-limited causes from those requiring urgent referral.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply gi manifestations reasoning for Cystic Fibrosis (GI/Pancreatic Manifestations).
candidates.source_competency_text: Recognize CF's GI/pancreatic manifestations (meconium ileus in the newborn, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency causing steatorrhea and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive) and the role of newborn screening and sweat chloride testing in diagnosis.

candidates.principal_decision: Apply workup reasoning for Iron Metabolism and Iron Deficiency Anemia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Identify the underlying source of iron loss (e.g., occult GI bleeding, menorrhagia, malabsorption) and initiate appropriate investigation by age/risk factors.
candidates.study_unit: Iron Metabolism and Iron Deficiency Anemia

candidates.principal_decision: Apply investigation reasoning for Syncope and Loss of Consciousness (Cardiac Differential).
candidates.source_competency_text: Select appropriate initial workup (ECG, orthostatic vitals, echocardiogram where indicated).
candidates.study_unit: Syncope and Loss of Consciousness (Cardiac Differential)

candidates.principal_decision: Apply ascites diagnosis reasoning for Ascites.
candidates.source_competency_text: Diagnose the cause of ascites using the serum-ascites albumin gradient (transudative vs. exudative) and initiate appropriate management (e.g., sodium restriction, diuretics, paracentesis for SBP work-up).

candidates.principal_decision: Apply dyspepsia approach reasoning for Dyspepsia.
candidates.source_competency_text: Differentiate ulcer from non-ulcer (functional) dyspepsia, identify alarm features requiring endoscopy, and initiate an empiric or test-and-treat management plan.
